I was actually talking about this with someone else one this forum. Think of FTR's as the flag limits. I have attached a chart with engulfs and the following flag limits marked with purple arrows. Notice how price "stair steps its way up?" When one of the limits gets engulfed that is your clue as to where price wants to go! When a whole zone gets engulfed you will be amazed at how price will respect them on the way down. Notice how price is compressed while in the zones? I think the trick is to watch the extremes of these zones and look for PA on smaller time frames for confirmation. Good luck, H Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Yes, we need to find space otherwise, there is no trade. If it was easy to find space, then everyone would become a successful trader overnight. The ITs will not make it easy and obvious. Trading is based on your preference and your comfort zone and your confidence in your analysis. There are master traders who take touch trades and take confirmation trade. It all depends on the trade itself. First, I would suggest you get comfortable with confirmation trades before jumping to touch trade. Confirmation trades will provide you more winners and put money in the bank for you. It will also build your confidence. Touch trading can be tricky, so you need to read the market correctly.... . You need to know if the level it is reacting to is the true supply..... you need to know how it reacted when it reached that level....., for example did price impulsive move away from that level and engulf an important FL to its left without hitting TG. If so, you have PA.. Now you want to see how price is retracing and approaching your entry point.(in this example, I am describing a QM)...... is it compressing, is it compressing and then a final impulsive move to your entry level....These are the questions that you need to answer. The 1/2 page on article on price reading in Marketpedia speaks it all. So, I would recommend you reading it over and over again until you truly understand. If you have any question, then you can post them and other students will help answer. Thanks for your answer, it helps me. I end up having a good price reading skills, I think I got what are the mecanisms behind left shoulders, i understand why there is symetry in the market I understand the concepts and I think what is behind it. But I'm really psychologically challenged by these confirmation trades. I know myself, i'm cautious so I set myself a rule which is just take confirmation trade. But I find so few of them that I get very very psychologically challenged. To be honest, I expected a lot of QM on one pair on small timeframes... I think I'm gonna change the way I screen the market. I used to take one or two pairs at a time and focus on them all day long. I think that's not working for me. I'm gonna screen every pair I have every morning, asking myself: "Are we at a good HTF level or near that? If yes, monitor and wait for confirmation, if no, go on..." Maybe because retailers don't have to know too much details about the real market price. And another fact. If you have a proper data feed and you see that a level is fresh (on a institutional platform), do you think that your retailer broker will break that level so easy? Even if his ask line tested your level, they can't break every level as they want. They still have to have approximately the same feed like the institutional broker. So, if in your insituttional broker data feed a level is holding price down i dont think the retailed broker will break that level by 100 pips. Sure, it could happen, but most of the time not. I think with a proper data feed you can be absolute certain that you have fresh orders inside a level or not and this can give you a massive edge. Until then i will try to use a broker which offer me the tightest spread in the universe. Anyway, its interesting to do a study about how ask price affect a level. EDIT: or why dont trying to sell at ask line, at least mental selling. When we see that the ASK line hit our level we can try to enter early by 0.1, 0.2 pips. The following user(s) said Thank You: cuimingzhao Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 16 Jun 2017 01:45 #2652 Manu --> Offline Trader Posts: 36 Thank you received: 47 Ok, I will try too. I see the symmetry as floors of a building where the price goes from one to another. Imagine that the price is a ball. A ball may bounce upward on the floor or down on the ceiling of a floor. But this ball also has the ability to cross the floor or ceiling if given circumstances. The rule is that the ball will only bounce (if it does) on the floor or ceiling of the floor where it is at the moment (not in the space between them wich is the floor itself), and if it crosses for example the ceiling and goes upstairs, the inertia will take it to the roof of that new floor (target). Then it could bounce there or cross that roof at first touch and move to the next floor. That is, if the price comes from below, the ceiling of new floor to which it accedes will be the target Let's see the chart: The price (ball) reaches the roof of the first floor and does not bounce, it crosses. We have left the first floor behind and we are already on the second floor. What happens here? The price begins to rebound on the roof and the floor several times until finally it crosses the ceiling and goes to the third floor. The price has already left the second floor and will not be able to cross it back until it reaches the roof of the third floor (target).What do we have on the second floor? A FLAG. Which are its limits? The floor and ceiling of the second floor. Floors and ceilings are FLs and can be FTRs, S/R, etc, too. I supose that at he left the ceilings and floors are respected, too. What happens on the third floor? Reaches the ceiling and directly crosses (line 3) to the fourth floor, so it must go to the ceilong of that new floor (target). What happens on the fourth floor? The ball (price) bounces a couple of times on ceiling and floor and crosses the floor returning to the floor below (third floor). As I said before, the price can only bounce off the floor and ceiling. As it comes from the ceiling, where could it bounce? On the floor, which is in turn the second floor ceiling. And so on. So what conclusion can we draw from this symmetry? The price will always bounce off the ceiling or floor and not anywhere else inside the floor. Therefore, WE ONLY MUST PLAN THE TRADES AT FLOOR OR CEILING OF THE FLOOR IN WHICH WE FIND US. OR WHAT IS THE SAME, IN THE FLs, FTR, etc. The engulf of one floor with a Flag inside will shoe us intentions to continue in the direction of the engulf. In the future, this structure of floors will be respected and the importance of each floor depend on what you have in the past on that floor PD: It is possible that everything I have said is nothing but nonsense. And i know that my english sometimes sucks, sorry for that. Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 21 Jun 2017 15:30 #2663 TheBeard --> Offline User is blocked Posts: 242 Thank you received: 242 Have you watched Peter Davies webinar on order flow? He uses the floors and ceilings analogy too. Manu wrote: Ok, I will try too. I see the symmetry as floors of a building where the price goes from one to another. Imagine that the price is a ball. A ball may bounce upward on the floor or down on the ceiling of a floor. But this ball also has the ability to cross the floor or ceiling if given circumstances. The rule is that the ball will only bounce (if it does) on the floor or ceiling of the floor where it is at the moment (not in the space between them wich is the floor itself), and if it crosses for example the ceiling and goes upstairs, the inertia will take it to the roof of that new floor (target). Then it could bounce there or cross that roof at first touch and move to the next floor. That is, if the price comes from below, the ceiling of new floor to which it accedes will be the target Let's see the chart: The price (ball) reaches the roof of the first floor and does not bounce, it crosses. We have left the first floor behind and we are already on the second floor. What happens here? The price begins to rebound on the roof and the floor several times until finally it crosses the ceiling and goes to the third floor. The price has already left the second floor and will not be able to cross it back until it reaches the roof of the third floor (target).What do we have on the second floor? A FLAG. Which are its limits? The floor and ceiling of the second floor. Floors and ceilings are FLs and can be FTRs, S/R, etc, too. I supose that at he left the ceilings and floors are respected, too. What happens on the third floor? Reaches the ceiling and directly crosses (line 3) to the fourth floor, so it must go to the ceilong of that new floor (target). What happens on the fourth floor? The ball (price) bounces a couple of times on ceiling and floor and crosses the floor returning to the floor below (third floor). As I said before, the price can only bounce off the floor and ceiling. As it comes from the ceiling, where could it bounce? On the floor, which is in turn the second floor ceiling. And so on. So what conclusion can we draw from this symmetry? The price will always bounce off the ceiling or floor and not anywhere else inside the floor. Therefore, WE ONLY MUST PLAN THE TRADES AT FLOOR OR CEILING OF THE FLOOR IN WHICH WE FIND US. OR WHAT IS THE SAME, IN THE FLs, FTR, etc. The engulf of one floor with a Flag inside will shoe us intentions to continue in the direction of the engulf. In the future, this structure of floors will be respected and the importance of each floor depend on what you have in the past on that floor PD: It is possible that everything I have said is nothing but nonsense. In order to do so, they cannot move the market fast, otherwise everyone will just buy and price shoots too far - REMEMBER: For ITs to buy they need sellers and vice versa. Therefore from my graph: 1. I as IT moved the price slowly back up to the supply (with CP) and added SELL orders throughout the CP. 2. As the price reached the previous H & S (QM) level, i let it stall for a while making them believe I am adding more buy orders at the same time Sellers see Double Top pattern and are ready to sell. 3. At the supply QM level, I remove my buy orders and price moves down making Sellers jumping on the wagon. 4. I suprise them and push the price back to FO level (There are now greedy buyers on board, and Double top sellers on board + This last push up to FO also invites late buyers as they believe its the start of new "trend") I noticed, it was easier to make this chart than reading the chart from MT4 lol... To answer a PM I got, which was "Is there any way to know how far will the retrace will happen after the break of the level?" No.It can retrace to any set of clean orders in the zone it's traveled through. Ideally it will travel all the way back for a QM at the MPL, or even break the H/L for a DM, but it often only retraces a short way, leaving the clean orders beyond for later. At each minor level it retraces to, we can take confirmed LTF trades, taking some profits to cover losses, letting some run to the HTF target, should this be the depth of the RT Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. The following user(s) said Thank You: PinkPanter , cuimingzhao Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 18 Jul 2017 05:37 #2744 Rinehart --> Away Associate Trader Posts: 450 Thank you received: 927 PinkPanter wrote: the other BIG mistery is NEWS releases, who buys in that milisecond, so the price spike up directly into supply and reverses and goes in other direction than big news pole? if they know that price will bounce why they buy it?? PinkPanter, news releases works almost exactly the opposite way most people imagine. The big spikes that happen right before and during a news release are rarely caused by ITs dropping massive orders and then reversing their orders with even more massive orders the other way. What often happens is that some IT's (since ITs trade different time frames too) remove their orders from the market. This causes a vacuum of orderflow where price moves to find new equilibrium. When we are talking about a spike to supply, there was more demand than supply once IT pulled their orders. This allows the sharp move higher to strong supply or an area with lots of retail buy stops (because IT takes opposite of retail). Then price falls because of overwhelming supply. I think there is a lot of ambiguity in this diagram and a lot of variables too. Firstly, is this an MPL of a FL or is a QM in a swing as a reaction to another FL/kink? If it is a QM, then price can make a diamond up to the MPL of a FL from above. The problem with diamonds and QM is that you can rarely find an engulf which hasn't hit its target so you have to gamble on them a little bit, i think. So, knowing that you can't find a engulf which hasn't hit its target nowadays, its definitely almost impossible to take gambling out of equation even when you trade BSZ. You have two important things to think about when you try to score your BSZ trade: - FLAG(BSZ) not touching the kink (so you can take FTB to that kink), and an engulf down (which is impossible to find it nowadays). So basically, from what i have seen in my study in forex tester, i cant expect more than 60% P/L ratio on these things and often the initial R is less than 1:1 because your kink is larger than your BSZ FO zone. If you want high R you have to be more agressive and i dont know, i think P/L ratio will drop down even more. Maybe i do something wrong but this is how i see it now. We have to deal with losses. I think i do something wrong, but so far this is how i see it. And regarding range filling, how can you expect for a range to be filled if you have no engulf which hasn't hit its target, you are not at the QM zone, and even if you are, price can make a diamond to an MPL of the FL from above which is 2TB to it now, so its risky. For me I have a complete strategy based on inferences I have made based on IFs teachings. Training my eyes to see the order-flow/manipulation really helped. Opening a chart and just seeing the clusters of different behavior really helped me. In regards to ranges etc. Its just a game of ping pong. Classically, IF would teach price moves from FL to FL. This has slightly changed in recent times with another method the ITs use for entries and targets as well. Everything in between the above and below level in that scale is a potential range to be filled. I base nearly my entire price reading on this. I use smaller scales to ride it up or down. Although I know where the levels are located, I only trade the best ones. But I need to know where price is coming from and which level is in control on my higher scale(s). I never think in terms of QM, DM, CanCan anymore as it s only a byproduct of the order flow and manipulation. If I know where the true orders reside I couldnt care less if its a QM , diamond etc. It may be different for you guys but this was another step forward for me. The pattern itself is only a footprint. What lays beyond it is whats truly amazing. See below, here is another important point. If a flag completes, I have no use for it anymore . In the picture IF posted, when he talked about dealers (or IT) that needs to fill a range, he most likely refer to a HTF range as depicted in my drawing below. So imagine on a HTF scale, price has already established a range from A to B. So when IT bring the price back to C, the movement from B to C is called 'filling the range'. Likewise, movement of C to D, and then from D back to E, are all called filling the range. Best regards Astro Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. I hope I understand you correctly, but here goes: The FL can only be drawn if price hit it's target means that if price doesn't retrace back far enough, it's not hitting the FL below and therefore it's no new FL but price just goes beyond it. There are several targets for price in several stages of it moving. The target for a new FL, is the FL below (or above) it and that has to be hit. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 14 Nov 2017 19:00 #3156 HCDE --> Offline Associate Trader Posts: 471 Thank you received: 648 I tried to take the exercise on and began to elaborate some scenarios. NB: i had to reproduce IF's drawing and made a clean version of it i join to the post in case other people want to use it for their scenarios It made me realize something important that i missed. I tried many times to spot engulfs into a FL (opposed to engulf of a FL). But when doing that i was considering in the same way a break in between two targets Inside the FL than a break in between the S/R kink of the FL and the first iLS. This is a mistake, because by breaking S/R kink and reaching first iLS, price reaches it's TG and therefore validates a new UFL Any break of that UFL is actually PA UP... So in that situation we shouldn't expect price to retrace to the UFL we came from and then get further into the LFL... Lesson learned. Then we follow breaking of that FL and mark the FLs to the right and so on. Image 2 shoes where we simply mark a kink(FL1) which held price up, which hits target(Red HTF FL), then breaking these FL will create the other FLs to the right. If we follow these two approaches, we will not end up with the same set of FLs. Another question is that, What is the important level in the first image X or what X is reacting to? Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 29 Mar 2018 05:50 #3444 bobyv87 --> Offline Associate Trader Posts: 326 Thank you received: 311 Its very difficult, if not impossible to give signals using RTM reading way. Why? Because even the right level can be FOed. So, knowing that, we always should have hard stops somewhere, but we don't wait for the hard stop to be hit, instead, after price break our level (fail level), we exit right at the next chance, when price bounce back to our fail level so we can exit without loss. Now, imagine that every level could have inside a few fresh orders. Would you wait always for MPLs inside each levels? If yes, you will miss a lot of opportunities. Would you wait lower than MPL? Maybe you wouldn't have the chance to exit at BE if your level fails. So, you have to take quick decisions, even if you have a good level and a good signal. At the same LSK IF can take a BE or a small profit, but in the same time others can take losses. Because of these multiple factors, its very difficult to do that. And imagine how much pressure you can put on IF with that. However, i'm planning to create a group of traders soon on the whatsapp, formed with those who can participate at meetings daily and share our setups for the day together so we can all benefit of our setups. :) Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 09 Apr 2018 11:39 #3454 Atari --> Offline Associate Trader Posts: 146 Thank you received: 389 We are our greatest enemy. The inner voice that is between our ears manages to take over all the time, bombarding us with excuses, with negative thoughts, shoot us down, telling us we cannot make it....etc..... Unless, we are aware that it is the inner voice talking and not us, then we can conquer and shut it up for the time being. It will want to come back and it is our job to notice it and shut it up again. When you catch it and shut it up, eventually, it will lose its grip on your mind. It is not gone, but it loses its power over you. Yes, RTM is a puzzle and you will have to put the puzzle together yourself here. Trading is not easy, but it is simple, once you get it. If trading is easy, then your garbage collector will be doing it too and you will not have anyone to pick up your garbage every week or day from your house. If Thomas Edison gave up on the 100th trial of creating a light bulb, do you think we will have a light bulb today? Thomas Edison had more than 1000 trial and error before you was able to invent the light bulb. If Steve Job and his team decided it was too difficult to create an Ipod/Ipad after months working on it, do you think we will have an Ipod/Ipad today. Success takes hard work and a spirit not to quit, no matter what obstacles are in front of us. You fall down, you get up, you fall down, you get up, you fall down you get up. We all forget that we are all champions when we were a baby. We all forgot that. Remember, when you were a baby learning how to stand and walk. When you fell down, you got right back up and try again and again and again, until you were able to walk and then run after. You did not tell yourself then, when you were a baby that it was too hard to learn to walk. You just got right back up and went at it until you got it. What makes you any difference now? It is your inner voice that is between your ears. You are listening to the negative messages it is feeding you. That is the difference. If you truly want to become a trader, then you must realize that and conquer it. Here is a question for you to ponder at. "If trading is the only thing I am committed to do, what would I do differently today?" Let me give you a story... A long time ago, there was a war between 2 countries. The captain was given 100 men to sail on his wooden ship to the enemy shores and take over that area. The enemy had 1000 men waiting for them. As soon as the captain landed and his men disembarked the wooden ship, the captain burned the ship. His men were left with the message, 'you can either choose to die here or defeat your enemy and live. His men did not have the comfort of retreating back to their ship for it has been burned. So either die at the enemy shore or defeat the 1000 men and take over and live. His 100 men at the end defeated the 1000.enemies. So if you come to RTM with that kind of mentality, your chances of success is much greater. You all know that we do have RTM Academy, which we put the puzzle together for you so that you don't have to spend thousands of hours trying to figure it out yourself. Even inside the academy, the students there have to roll up their sleeves and work hard on the lessons and assignments and learn how to think critically and apply their analytical skills. While the price tag may cause some of you to shy away from it, I can for certain say that the value you will get from the Academy will easily overshadow the price tag once you graduate from the Academy. Hi Scipio As I see it, I'll be remaking all the material that's already here on RTM, relating it all to the revelations I got over the last year. I also have other revelations to add (let me stress once again, that all these revelations I got were based on the lessons I already gave, and can be had by anybody who ties all the lessons together!) The lessons will be structured in such a way that each makes a strong foundation for the next Students would be given homework assignments on the lessons, and once we're satisfied they know the material, they'd get access to the next lessons. There'll be regular tutorial webinars intended to tie the lessons together. As I see it, there will probably be two modules to the course - one for reading price, and one for trading. Access to the trading section would be granted to those who've graduated from the reading module In it I'd be explaining everything about chart setup, trade selection, trade management, and trading plan construction. There are a number of types of trade, and a myriad of trader lifestyles, temperaments and time limitations, so this section will give the students the trading rules which will work best for them. These trading plans will take much of the emotion out of trading, making their job mechanical. There'll be a lot of personal attention put into each student, but for those who want to book extra one on one time, there may be packages on offer to cover this There'll be final exams for each of the modules, and qualifications awarded to the graduates. There will be a forum for students, and a forum for alumni I'm sure I'm leaving loads out here, but this is the essence of it Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. In a market like forex, where there are real big players who need to buy and sell huge amount of currencies, I am of the opinion that the very fundamental approach of order flow, supply and demand can never change they way dealers work. So will they change their methods, I am not too sure. But where I am sure is they can trick us, false breakouts, diamonds,..... and perhaps many ways that I am not experienced to know yet. I started on this trail to RTM, courtesy of Sam Seiden. He thought something very interesting, very fundamental and very simple. Not easy to trade but simple and beautiful in concept and practice. A little diversion, I find him and his team very frustrating. They would always show you the supply and demand zones but they never show you the further left side of charts in deciding why they pick one zone and not the other. The originators of RTM, and a couple of other kind souls out there have shown me the other details that sam seiden and his commercial team have always left out. For that I, for the rest of my life here on earth am very indebted to you all. Thank you very much and I am very interested in this RTM academy project. FB It really does make you wonder. The parts departments of these garages will grow, while the service departments will dwindle. Now, the number of retail traders is growing rapidly. At the moment, most of them are being taught pure rubbish by fraudsters, or pure lies by brokers. But as more and more traders get educated, which is bound to happen, there just may not be enough orders against the big guys' buys or sells, so they'd be forced to push price further and further, or turn price earlier. All this we'll be able to read of course. Wrong! The market is run by people who know what they're doing. They use a finite number of tools to trick retailers into offering orders up to them. They use a finite number of algorithms to do their work for them. In order to avoid chaos, they have rules they abide by (honour amongst thieves) Once you learn these tricks, how to spot these algorithms, and the rules they obey, you will be in the mind of the market makers, and you can trade just as they do 2: I have played with indicators until I have worn them out, they are lagging in price and can not either predict or work. Absolutely! The Market Movers know these indicators too! 3: PA together with Supply and Demand is king. PA at important S/D S/R levels is key. Price history tells you which are important 4: Money Management is a top priority. No one can out run, predict or me smarter than the market. Money management IS key. But it's not difficult to out run, predict and be smarter than the market 5: Always respect higher time frames in respect of placing trades on lower time frames. Very true 6: If an acceptable set up is seen calculate the risk to reward ratio (this should be 3:1 at a minimum) 3:1 is a very very low number, but it's OK to begin with 7: Before entering in any trade make sure there is a bullish or bearish candle confirmation present. Forget about candles. It's engulfs that are important 8: Place stop losses accordingly and and move to break even at the earliest opportunity. This is a massive subject. But in essence: If you're not at the screen, do put your stop losses beyond true S or D. But know that price will so very often retrace to pick up extra orders. This leads on to your next problem - the retrace is there to take out your break even. If you fear the BE hunt, get out at TG1 and take the trade there again if the setup looks good 9: Patience is a virtue (one area I fail in badly) Amen to that!!!! 10: I can not seem to stick to one style of system, this I find very frustrating and another of my bad traits. ITs need liquidity to enter and exit the market, and they have the wealth to 'send signals' that manipulate beliefs in retail traders and herd them into areas where they effectively trade against the ITs... . Yes patterns do repeat and can be used as short-hand, and brains are great at spotting patterns, and ITs know this, and that's why patterns repeat... . (And just to misquote Mark Twain, "Patterns do not repeat themselves, but they sure do rhyme.".) Here's my attempt at If's quiz, I'm not saying my observations are correct (and they may even be completely wrong), but they show how I try to think when I'm looking at a chart. It is much much easier to give reasons why price should have turned at an area when you already know that it did, it's not so easy on the hard right edge (at least not for me!), and we don't know what was going on before we see these patterns (they may be reactions to Supply and Demand areas). Warning: Spoiler! [ Click to expand ] [ Click to hide ] The notes are a bit jumbled but read them in numerical order: Caveat lector! (And if I'm truly wide of the mark, help wouldn't be turned away ) Regards. Spongy. Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. Anyways I don't consider it a FO in terms of order flow and change in direction. A Fakeout has 3 goals: to take out SL of opposite trades, to reach a better SD zone beyond this SD zone or SR level, to take orders of breakout traders. - Who is short at that level (and where is their SL)? I think not so many. So no stop loss hunt. - Do this FO reached a better Supply zone to go short? Actually no, there is a fresh level at origin of the downmove but the price didn't touch it. - Who is trading a breakout? there isn't a good level to attract breakout traders in the near. For these reasons for what we see in this picture (we can't look to the left) I don't think point A is a good level for placing a FO. Imo it can be considered an engulf and price will go higher and maybe reverse at that fresh level up there. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 19 Nov 2013 19:05 #602 Pedini --> Offline Master Trader Posts: 568 Thank you received: 2602 madwt wrote: Hi IF, FO or Engulf? Some people have interpreted the break of "A" as an engulf, yet others have interpreted it as a fake out. In this post you were asked what is the difference between an engulf and a fake out. No answer was provided. I understand that an engulf involves price making a lower low on reaction to Supply, or higher high on reaction to Demand. More importantly, it shows intent of price to continue in the direction of the engulf . I also understand that a fake out occurs in order to find sufficient liquidity to sell/buy against. More importantly, it is followed by a change in direction . Knowing if the break of "A" is an engulf or fake out requires analysis of the complete picture (higher time frames and looking left). However, as neither of these are provided in the quiz, its mere speculation. Taking the following chart as an example, would this be interpreted as an engulf or as a fake out of "A" (or is it possible to be both)? What is the difference between an engulf and fake out. Thanks, d Hi Buddy, "I understand that an engulf involves price making a lower low on reaction to Supply, or higher high on reaction to Demand" - This can be correct, but it certainly is not always correct, actually most of the time it isn't correct. You need to find the important engulfs of flags, it is when these happen that an engulf becomes meaningful. Simply making a higher high or lower low will not show you any intent. Also understand that an engulf will achieve the same thing as a FO (in terms of retailer trading behaviour) but it is the signal that price wants to go to the next important level in the direction of the engulf. A FO is simply a ploy to trap traders once the signal engulf has already happened. Study up on flag limits, there has been some very good posting on them recently, understanding the FL and the engulfs of the FL's along with a HTF analysis and you will be able to tell the FO from the Engulf. Sorry if that was a little bit of a mouthful, Peds Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. On the topic for tonight's management meeting is why I haven't resolved it yet, so I'd better get in here and answer it before I get a rollicking :) So let's get to it: 1. The leading IT engulfed price back up into the range (engulfed V), showing he was taking price up to the last FL above (U) 2. The other ITs, who had been short from high above, saw that price had turned, and wanted out of their shorts and into long positions. So they sold against the retail breakout long trades They will have Faked Out below a ltf demand (not visible in this tf), scaring the BO buyers into selling at a loss, and enticing BO sellers, giving them lots to buy against and go net long. 3. A marker was set for future use 4. They turned price before the target, creating a supply which could be broken later 5. Price had been dropping for some time, attracting lots of retail sellers; the IT's were eating these up bit by bit. It was obvious to the more savvy of the retailers that price was heading for W. So the natural thing to do was turn price before the tg, creating a demand to be faked later. They buy heavily, taking all the herd's sells and shooting price back up. 6. They removed their pending orders at 4, allowing price to break supply. All the short retailers freak out and start closing by buying. This allows the ITs to sell to them, beginning the process of going from long to short. 7. They begin to flag price downwards, adding little shorts as they create LLs and LHs. This of course means a downtrend to the retailers, so the retailers begin selling too 8. The Its want to be the only sellers, so they buy heavy into Supply (U) shaking out the retail sellers and enticing BO buyers, all giving them more to sell to The retailers are getting frustrated by now. In the chop, there are lots of losers buying and selling all over the place, taking revenge trade after revenge trade. With prices still making HHs and HLs though, very many are still buying Savvy SD retailers, however, are selling at 8, putting their stops above (U) (poor beggars!). As price rises through supply, these SD retailers are adding to their shorts, delighted to get even better prices, and the ITs are happy to let them do so, because at 9. The ITs have either once again removed their pending short orders in Supply, or have used them to tentatively buy against. By adding different sizes of orders, they can now feel, by how price reacts to their orders, who's in the market with them. They feel when the selling pressure has dropped, and take this opportunity to buy just enough to break the supply. This hits the savvy SD retailers' stops and entices tons of BO buys, giving them masses of buyers for the sells they're ready to make. They're now heavily short. 10. They take some profit, creating a demand to be broken later 11. It's important that they bewilder every retailer out there; tire them out completely so they have no idea what they're doing. So they retrace price back up, breaking LTF supplies as they go, attracting more buyers. Price hasn't engulfed anything south yet, so the once savvy SD retailers are buying too, trying to reclaim their losses. The ITs are selling to them in bits, until they feel the buyers have dwindled enough for them to put in their next set of big shorts, breaking 10 at 12. They buyers stops have hit, and the remaining BO sellers are getting in, giving the ITs a breather. They're heavily short, and happy. 13. We're at the SR of 4. ITs take a little profit, bouncing price up a bit, breaking a LTF supply. This gets the retail sellers out, offering more buys for the IT to sell to 14. It's the same story as 6 and 9 15. The FO to the Demand of the FL. It would be remiss of any IT not to take full advantage of all the shorts on offer here, and cause some midrange mayhem! 16. The engulf - time to flag 17. Create Supply before tg to be broken later 18. Inverse of 17 19. Chop for some confusion now and levels to be broken later 20. Sell to the BO buyers and SD sellers' stops 21. Lots more easy BO and stop orders to be snatched up. This is real fun for the ITs, and is having little effect on their overall position size in the big picture, until they want it to! 22. Catches lots more of the usual losers and fills the range Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. Albert Einstein Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 12 Feb 2013 23:06 #69 Ifmyante Topic Author --> Offline Chief Cook and Bottle Washer If you see a piece of truth glistening in the dirt, get down on your knees and gently dig it out, for it's the greatest treasure you will ever find Posts: 3574 Thank you received: 14393 This perhaps should be the first thing that anybody ever reads regarding trading: We're always looking for signs of what the big guys are doing at significant areas, and if we don't see what they're doing, there's no trade So, on approach, if we see the big guys trying to hide their orders in the market, we see compression, and can feel pretty sure of their intentions - to get in as many orders as they can before the turn If we don't see this, we can be pretty sure that it won't just turn immediately, as there usually won't be enough orders against them to fill all the orders they must fill. This is why we wait for an engulf. This shows their intention to reverse price. Then we watch them trying to hide their orders in the market on a retrace, ready to take price to the origin of the move Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. This is why we wait for an engulf. This shows their intention to reverse price. Then we watch them trying to hide their orders in the market on a retrace, ready to take price to the origin of the move I'll interpret what you said above to ensure I understand it properly, because I believe this is crucial. I'll use two examples to illustrate my interpretation. Apologies for polluting your journal. If price compresses to, let's say, supply, the big guys are already giving away their intentions. For arguments sake, if compression is perfect (no demand left behind), then that's the only signal you need. Trade as soon as you get a few candles rejecting higher highs. YOU DON"T NEED CONFIRMATION (??) (That's my first question) BECAUSE COMPRESSION IS ENOUGH TO DISCLOSE BIG MONEY'S INTENTIONS. The example below is PA on the EURUSD. Compression into supply was nearly perfect. Do we wait for the retest after the engulfing or can we enter as soon as the euro prints the rejection bar? (I ask this because if there is no demand left, price will unlikely return for a retest of the break, right?) When price doesn't compress to, let's say, supply, then we will need some kind of signal that reveals big money's intentions. The signal is the engulf. Then we wait for a retest of left over supply, or break of flag or resistance. The example below is recent PA in the EURGBP. IF, is this the correct way to interpret your quote? Keep watching how FLs shift around the screen, and someday you'll be able to profit from what you've learned Thanks IF, But this brings about a couple more questions regarding PA and stops. Now when it comes to levels and stops, I was always under the belief that if a new level was created during active market hours within your zone, then that becomes your new trade/ risk area. A little unwritten rule of thumb that I have myself is that at least a new 1hr, 30 min, or 15 min embedded zone has to be created for me to make that my NEW trade/ risk area upon revisit since higher TFs are more reliable. Here is an example of a trade I took yesterday on the CADCHF. 1hr 4hr As you can see, the trade I took was a plane jane trade that was simply based off of the 4hr zone that cause the consumption of upper supply. Since we were still clearly in an uptrend with a plausible 4hr target overhead yet to be hit, I figured I would go for it even though we didn't get the full engulf. The trade worked out fine, but in the LTFs, I watched the action develop, and a setup that I have always considered valid came up. Here is the setup I'm talking about as previously mentioned in the first two paragraphs, 1hr As you can see, there was a new 1hr demand zone that was created WITHIN my 4hr zone during the active market hours. In my mind, this was a high probability trade which I would have probably taken on the retest if I wasn't already in the trade. My logic for this is if a NEW 1hr demand zone was created when pro money was active, then why have my stop beyond the original 4hr zone? Whey not enter on the retrace to the newly created 1hr demand and have your stop below that? That is the same logic I had in my EURGBP trade, so assuming we did get the proper PA and engulfed the 1min FO level, why would my stop still need to be below the original zone you showed since this would have been a NEW 1hr demand zone within the 4hr demand?? The way I have always looked at it, playing PA to the right like this increases RR and I have seen it work a hundred times before in my studies. As for the TP, it would have stayed the same for me (the 'ultimate profit target' in the 4hr chart) since this was a new 30 min or greater embedded demand zone. If this were just a newly created 15 min demand zone, I would have switched to 'intraday' mode and my ultimate TP would have been more conservatively based upon the lower 4hr zone that caused the retrace. Also, with regard to PA, I personally have a problem with zooming all the way down to the 1min to check for the limits to be engulfed because when you get down that low, it seems you can always make a case (or a least most times) as to whey 'this' or 'that' 1min zone is the reason price is being held down. It can just get very messy, confusing, and paralyzing when you go down that low to look for confirmation because there are rarely places in the chart where one will have a complete liquidity gap/ pole down to the 1 min. If I were to scrutinize every trade I took to this level, well, I don't think I would ever take a trade because this is a perfect setup and the market rarely provides those in my eyes, which is why we have stops in the first place. Sorry for these long drawn out questions, but I feel these are key issues I have been battling with for a while now without avail. Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Find the source, trade it- SyT Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 25 Oct 2014 17:41 #938 Ifmyante Topic Author --> Offline Chief Cook and Bottle Washer If you see a piece of truth glistening in the dirt, get down on your knees and gently dig it out, for it's the greatest treasure you will ever find Posts: 3574 Thank you received: 14393 In response to a pm I got this morning: Lately I had a man-cold, and for a while during that time I'd open the chart and feel I had no idea what I was looking at. I knew I knew the market, but there was still something inside me telling me that I wouldn't be able to read it This wasn't upsetting at all , because I knew full well this malady would pass and I'd be back on top of it again. This can happen to anybody, due to illness, fatigue, fear of failure, fear of success, or any number of other causes. For a student this can be very distressing and debilitating. But it need not be terminal. The problem is not that one's read has gone. The loss of the read is just a manifestation of another problem in life. That's why, when we lose it, we must step away from the charts, and look within ourselves to find the unresolved issues. Once we've faced and fixed them, we can get straight back to work in a better state than if we never had the problem in the first place I remember when I was learning the market, I'd have these EUREKA moments, which were wonderful! I'd think to myself "I've got it! I've got it!" and imagine that now everything I did would be perfect from then on. But it wasn't. I'd still not be right all the time. Soon I'd get another eureka moment, and think I had it again. But no. There are a number of lessons which need to be learned, and each helps. Then, as price returns to a supply or demand formed at or near the zone identified in Step 1, a touch trade or confirmed trade can be taken. 4. Place the stop beyond the edge of the zone identified in Step 1; target 1 is the next demand or supply in the LTF used, while the final target is the original of the move to the zone identified in Step 1, often the next demand or supply in that HTF used. The reason you wanted us to put the puzzle pieces together instead of handing over the golden keys is for us to accumulate the chart experiences (screen hours), and figure out what HTF and LTF would work, and to form the psychology to follow the plan. Find your own light.” Posts: 129 Thank you received: 244 Guys, FL is the two lines/zones that 'enclose' the flag area like a sandwich. The bread is the limit, Not the egg inside. I remember that we must find setup on the edge, which in this case the 'Flag Limit' itself, not inside the flag. The edge where the price break later become the new DP point for price to return to. It MUST break important key levels before you can consider its value. That's my half cent. Please kindly correct me if I'm wrong. Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. I only found RTM at the end of September. For the first month, I was trying to "predict" what was going to happen, by analysing the charts down to the finest detail, and simple to say, I failed miserably, due to lack of experience in such things. But does that mean I can't trade, and trade very successfully with the things taught on here? No, not at all. My biggest strides forward came when I gave up trying to predict what was going to happen, and just let the market show me its intentions. Think you've spotted a level that price is going to turn at? Great, now wait and see what happens. Got a significant engulf off the level you want? Check again - was it really significant? Or has it just come down to a SR flip level to continue in the way it was already going? How is price moving? Has it shot up to your level with a single big candle? Has it compressed towards it? Has it proceeded up in a series of surges, forming fresh demand levels every step of the way? All we need to trade successfully is the ability to spot potential turning points ahead of time, and then just wait and see what happens when we get there. If we see things lining up in our favour, take the trade, and set your target at the first point you can realistically expect trouble from. Don't "expect" price to blow through several levels of strong supply or demand to some hollywood target. There are plenty of pips out there, if one would just be patient, and let the market tell us what it wants to do. Predicting huge moves, and setting POs ahead of time with pinpoint accuracy is something I'm sure I will be able to do with 100s more hours of chart time, but right now, I've got more than enough tools in my kit with the things that are taught on here to be profitable. Has it proceeded up in a series of surges, forming fresh demand levels every step of the way? All we need to trade successfully is the ability to spot potential turning points ahead of time, and then just wait and see what happens when we get there. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 12 Mar 2015 08:27 #1157 geejay --> Offline Trader PRICE ACTION WILL SHOW YOU THE WAY Posts: 41 Thank you received: 58 Hi J9, Sure. At point 1 on the down side, we have an engulf. The little flag on the left side is a decision, a decision to go higher and go back into the M15 flag. On the way down, when this level marked by the red line in broken, we can say the demand was engulfed. Next price flags. It bottoms, reverses back to the red line, then on the next wave down, it makes a lower low. To me, that is a clear signal that price wants to go lower. So, when price comes back to 3, to test the cap at 1, it is a good place to go short. And a point to clarify about QM. They do work in all timeframes, M1 up to MON1. What I was referring to is their respective locations. We are more interested in QM that form in historical S and D zones. So, the way you marked up your QM, was for a short. But I don't see any Supply zone there. There is supply for sure but the way I learned QM was to expect them at higher TF supply zones (Daily Supply for example for shorts). Perhaps the easiest is to go back to the QM article and read it again as that is probably clearer than my explanation. GJ. Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Profit or Loss, if a trade is identified and setup properly, and executed with proper risk management, thats a good trade. Even if it loses money (shit happens?). From what I am getting there is a strong relationship between the diamond, QM, price caps, and triple hit. These are all things that can happen at HTF zones. The CORE of what we are looking for is to find a HTF supply or demand that has history and been engulfed in one direction or the other. Then we are to zoom down to lower time frames and find the precise decision points that price turned and shot the other direction. These are called swap zones or decision points, right? When we are looking for decision points on smaller TF, they can be QM, diamonds, or price caps, right? In the end we are looking for flag poles on several time frames. Below are some charts: The first chart is the 240min. Does it matter if I use the "yellow" line, or the solid one that the "blue" arrow is pointing to as the price that was engulfed on the way up? Next is the 60 min chart. The solid line is the same line that the "blue" arrow was pointing to on the 240min. Notice the swap level that the blue arrow is pointing to. Next is the 1 minute chart. The dashed line is the higher level from the 240min chart. Notice the flag that this line makes. Since the base of the pole is almost engulfed on this one, I rather look at the lower level. The lower solid line level is the lower level from the 240min chart. This level seems to also have a swap level that could be the base of a flag. That RBR is where I will look to enter. Is this right thinking? The last chart is what happened when price returned. Price did not seem to like that larger flag area that was the higher level on the 240min(price marked with dashed lines). Price did like that lower area that seemed to be a swap level on the 1min and the base to a flag pole. Is this thinking correct? Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 20 Jun 2015 12:03 #1364 Raj --> Offline Trader Posts: 6 Thank you received: 0 Hi Smimon: Here is my take on your diagram. When price engulfs your "more important FL" the logical expectation then would be a slide to the next demand zone which is the "Less important FL" in your chart. So, for me, price has reached its logical destination after the engulf or rather fakeout. I view it more as stacked demand and it is always better to wait for the price to reach the lower of the two stacked levels. The higher level is a prime case for faking-out. Whether you want to call the "Less important FL" as a FL or DP is again up to you. Just nomenclature I guess. Point is, there is pent-up demand in that area. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 28 Jun 2015 20:40 #1388 Rdk123 --> Offline Trader Posts: 282 Thank you received: 286 Hi Muffles, you make a very good point! Understanding this can give us a massive leap forward in our learning curve, especially when paired with a trained eye for spotting QM levels and important S/R. One thing I have noticed recently is the QM level flip, when a QM level fails it it actually turns in to a very well respected level on RT and even in the future, and If we check I guarantee it will have been in the past. The importance of how powerful S/R can been is shown in our QM levels, they even give a tradable bounce most of the time, like in your chart. Like you say, if the FO doesn't reach it's target then it's an engulf in to a new zone and we want the other side, this shows us what to expect from a QM level. I am no expert but after many hours of looking at the charts I am seeing price for what it is, for me, there are levels of perceived value running through the charts in every TF, these levels move up and down but we can follow them with our flag limits and to be honest even just a good eye for perceived value flipping. The more I look at the charts the more I think big money is lazy and that is why this is so simple, I imagine big money goes like this, 'If price is above X then it is worth Y, when it gets to Y I'll make a decision, If Y is to expensive it is worth X, If Y is still to cheap, it is worth Z but no less than X'. And because big money is so lazy, these perceived levels of value are pretty evenly spaced, probably to the pip if we really wanted to take the time to find out. I would like to take this opportunity to apologise to you IF and to be honest the rest of the teachers and authors of the training material, I'm not stubborn enough to not admit when I'm wrong, I went through a period of mental turmoil, which I'm sure many of the members here have at some point in trying to master this. The frustration was more with myself and I didn't really have anywhere to direct it when I hit a wall, taking time away actually really helped me, I had to visualize the charts in my head but I couldn't see the detail, this was the biggest aha moment of them all and I was no where near a screen. Anyway, I'm apologising for doubting what you have supplied here, I would also like to give my admiration for how you have stuck with this even through all of the grief you must receive from people. I don't really know you but I do respect the fact you give so much, expecting very little, if nothing in return. I hope you manage to read this, along with every other member who may have doubt. Trust what you see, I saw levels of perceived value and over layed the FTR, FL, diamond and QM on top of them, they all form on perceived levels of value, this is how we can get out of a failed trade at BE or better, by only trading these levels, I'm not saying it is easy but it works. Thank you all for your time. I'll be getting back to my journal this week with a calm approach and self control. Have a good Sunday all, Robbie Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Probably I overthink .. as always There are 8 main currencies in the Forex market. It is possible to calculate currency indexes for each one - but it's not a straight average across each currency's crosspairs. Instead, the trade figures for each currency are used, and the 5 most heavily traded opposing currencies are used for the index weighting calculation. For example, this is JPYX: From these figures, you can calculate a correctly balanced currency index for each currency. I have had these for some time now, I coded them up in MT4 (AUDX/CADX/CHFX/EURX/GBPX/JPYX/NZDX/USDX). When correctly balanced, RTM style setups work exactly the same on these composite charts - except it is an entire currency that is making a move. Institutional money tends to flow from one currency into another, they don't adopt a view on a single pair. For the best trades, you find separate currencies forming opposing setups - when 2 currencies are moving in opposite directions, the relevant crosspair totally flies. Some brokers carry USDX and EURX, but the balancings are usually incorrect or out of date. You can also find things like GBPX online on some websites, but the calculation is a straight average across all crosses. This is nonsense really, to attach the same weighting to GBPNZD as EURGBP when forming a GBPX index. When used correctly, these are a massive odds enhancer. You get double confluence by checking the 2 indexes for each cross, to see if it supports your trade. It keeps me out of a lot of bad decisions. It also helps keep you on the right side of the market if you always try to play strongest vs weakest. There's a good article here on ForexFactory about it www.forexfactory.com/showthread.php?t=334165 In answer to your AUD question - if AUD is strong on the day, but JPY is stronger, the other AUD pairs will move up, but AJ will chop around at its short zone. If JPY remains strong as AUD hits supply, then it will drop. You quite often see this, one of the crosspairs "hanging around" at supply or demand, waiting for the index to hit the appropriate level before it moves off. Here are the 8 currency indexes from today: i.imgur.com/2JiLOeN.png Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 16 Aug 2015 16:58 #1657 smimon --> Offline Trader Posts: 549 Thank you received: 1075 Yes that's spot on Gembel, that's exactly the way they should be used. Taking LTF trend continuations on pullbacks to FLs, based on the bigger picture strongest vs weakest currencies, as inferred from the indexes, is the highest probability way to make easy pips, or even better, getting in right at the top of the whole currency turn (although picking tops/bottoms is always going to be riskier somewhat). Where a lot of currency strength indis fail, and we can do better with them, is that in order to determine a currency's strength, they use some sort of moving average to determine the trend - simply "is it going up right now, or going down right now?" We however, with our knowledge of PA, could look at EURX and say "well, it's going up right now, but we've had a significant engulf south, and now we've pulled back to a QM level, so in fact I don't think it's strong, I think it's about to become very weak". In this cases, we can actually hit the market on the correct crosspairs at exactly the right moment that the crosspair is going to turn. Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Its a chart of the EUR/USD. FIrst off lets start with the flags. I think the definition of a flag is when the top and bottom are liquidity gaps. In other words you find the area on the bottom that was broken with strong demand and the area on the top that was broken with strong demand. The area in the middle is your flag or CP. Right? My flags on here are marked with blue rectangles. The red lines are the extremes that we would look for price action and the middle is where we don't want to diddle! In other words there is either really clean ignored/broken SD above and below the CP or its just a flag. This is why the other areas that I marked with trend lines are not flags. These areas are just CP, thats why price moved through them. I don't know however why price stopped at the yellow line. That demand was spiked. If you look at the flag at the top with the red arrow, that is where I would look to short. Its an engulf from the area just to the left of it. For now it looks like price is compressing back up to the flag that did the engulfing. This means that I would look at the red lines of that flag on lower time frames for a sign. This could be a swap level, QM, engulf, or it might CP into the edge. Is this right? Thanks, H Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. ShadowPit wrote: bobyv - I think you need to upload the chart with your additional markups to make sense of what you're asking The short answer to your question is Demand exceeded Supply at a level you have not drawn. My observations in black. Some general feedback using the chart for illustration: Be cautious with creating too higher expectation from one engulf or one observation you make. Trading requires consideration of multiple sources of information which may come from other time frames as well. Be careful not to expect price to make higher highs or lower lows, just because you identified an engulf of a level (note obstacle 1 & 2). Pay special attention to the QM level drawn on the chart, the level is more than a singular horizontal line, if you want to use just a single line, draw it under the lows of the "1" and "2". The QM level held price up on 4 occasions! On the 2nd, 3rd and 4th occasion it made a higher high on this timeframe. There was no engulf of this zone, therefore you cannot rely on your expectation that price would go any lower than this zone at any stage of your analysis. In fact if you look on from point "4" the simple observation that no supply was holding price down and new demand was being created would tell you that a sell off was highly unlikely. Also last but not least, let's just say you did enter a touch trade short based on your assertion that price engulfed the low you have identified, you have obstacle #1 immediately below you, reducing your probability of success. Hope this helps. Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You My Decision for gbp/jpy from h4 Chart 11 Oct 2015 09:41 #1755 ShadowPit --> Offline Associate Trader Posts: 277 Thank you received: 1195 boby, First: To me A&C have nuanced differences: C is a clean looking DBR, it sits above a key level (resistance becomes support), it isn't compressed, it moves cleanly away AFTER the break of a key level (strong imbalance). A doesn't have the same characteristics, it is a compressed move, it doesn't sit on top of a key level, it sits underneath a recent high, it is BEFORE the break of a key level, it does however have an ok move out of the level which eventually runs into the HTF supply extremes without retracement to a demand level, which C does not have this characteristic. Onto the move up: B is the supply (DBD) that caused the break of C (DEMAND) which sits at a key level. C could have just as easily bounced price back up, but it didn't. D does not have this same characteristic, it breaks nothing of significance, it only extends the move lower into demand, and is very promptly broken. Having said that, strong imbalance of price is implied at both B and D until price tells us otherwise and you cannot presume that price will break either until it does. In this case, D is broken without any retracement so we look to B if it can hold price down, but it doesn't, which can only mean price has paved the way for higher prices. As buyers flood the market, sellers are either trapped and wanting to get out as close to their failed entries (at B and D) as possible or face being stopped out. (this is the psychological makeup of the market) Price will now look higher to find better supply, price will go higher from most RECENT _fresh_ demand if it can, which happened to fall at the break of D (remember the imbalance has now been flipped). This is the origin. Remember, the break of D is the source of breaking D AND B, surely a stronger imbalance of price compared to if it was only the source of breaking D and NOT B.. Even better is that this origin is in CONFLUENCE with the original KEY LEVEL (C) which is textbook perfect S/R which is where you always want to be placing your trades. Hope this helps. Retailers just jump on it. So any swing H and L was specially made by ITs to get specific reactions (orders) by retailers. Obviously ITs move by imbalancing, then placing their sells/buys against retailers + imbalance necessary for the move (i think). in the upper part of the chart there are swings H & HH. Some Retailers sell immediately below H + stop above. ITs take all stop as BUY orders. Other Retailers buy immediately above H + stop below L. ITs take only orders, again BUY orders . Other Retailers have here Stop of sell orders placed below the L. ITs take all as BUY orders in the lower part of the chart there are swings L & LL Some Retailers buy immediately above L + stop below. ITs take all stop as SELL orders Other Retailers sell immediately below L + stop above H. ITs take only orders, SELL orders Other Retailers have here stop of buy orders placed above H. ITs take all as SELL orders So at the end of all cycles IT will have collected a number of closed BUY and SELL Stop Loss + orders it means also a predominance of BUY or SELL orders, when ITs consider that amount satisfactory, they will move against it. in that chart the predominance should be BUY retail orders, then we can expect a pole down. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 14 May 2016 19:55 #1939 Ifmyante Topic Author --> Offline Chief Cook and Bottle Washer If you see a piece of truth glistening in the dirt, get down on your knees and gently dig it out, for it's the greatest treasure you will ever find Posts: 3574 Thank you received: 14393 I've just been reading Deenius' journal, where I found the answers to pretty much every question I could ever be asked, so I'm stealing his fine work and putting it here deenius wrote: Ok, I would like to restart my journal with my favorite Ifmyante quotes. I think, it is really important stuff. Ifmyante quotes If the signal is given by the market mover (an engulf into a new zone), then price is very unlikely to break the extreme of the zone it just came from. So, if you have the patience to wait at the last remaining set of unfilled orders in the origin, you can be almost certain that that price will be respected. There is absolute order in the market. Nothing at all there happens by chance. That's why it's so easy to read what's going to happen next. There are rules which are strictly followed; so much so you'd imagine it's all run by algorithms, up to the moment when the signal is decided upon, and straight away thereafter. There is zero chaos in the market. It's elegantly designed; a beauty to behold. Fakeouts are extremely easy to predict. Most SD traders still look directly left, which is the big shortcoming of Supply/Demand trading. It's further left again we should be looking. Say price is coming up to a supply. The only way we can be sure that supply will hold price down is if that supply has already visited the extreme set of orders in the flag limit to its left. If the supply fell short of that, we can anticipate a FO to those extreme orders. Extremely simple stuff. We always look to what S or D are reactions to, rather than just S or D themselves. Look for tricks being played on approach to a place where a trick was played, and you'll find where price will turn. If you can look beyond S/D, you'll see that the Flag Limit is the only true place to look for PA for a trade. Trade these levels and you're taking gambling out of your method. All we can ever hope for is a bounce at these levels, unless we are certain that this level is the deepest possible point of retrace after a previous engulf. Without that, we must watch PA as it develops, both before and during the trade. Set and Forget trades can only be taken once the signal is given and the target is clear. Being patient is absolutely vital for making giant trades. We must wait for the very best possible places before we enter; the places where you'd expect great PA to react. If you're around to watch the PA unfold, it's rare your stop should get hit. Price will so very often retrace enough for you to get out without a loss. That's why I wait for the very best price to TT - it tends to keep me in the black. I'm not even a part time trader now, so I miss nearly every piece of action there is. If I ever open the charts and see a trade opp right in front of me, I take it. However, I usually get between 10R and 25R per trade. If I lose, it's usually no more than the spread and commission. There are between 5 and 20 such confirmed trades available every day. First of all, we need to understand that time has no place in any read of the market. The only way to be completely sure of where a FL is, is to be there when the break occurs, and mark the highs and lows as they occur. Within a minute they can be obscured by a candle, but we'll know exactly where they are. If we're not there to watch and mark, we must use the full candle as a FL. If we've had an engulf and are getting in on a RT, we must always be ready for a diamond to occur, especially if price hasn't yet hit MPL of the zone the original bounce was a reaction to. So, if we're not going to be around to watch PA, our stop must be beyond the original FL. Funny you should say that, as I teach to always and only trade within a flag. Sometimes the flag will already have developed, and sometimes the flag is to be made while you're in the trade. Either way, always trade within a flag. Attune yourself to what the buggers are doing, and don't let them fool you. Just know they've got orders to fill at a level, watch them fill some on approach (CP), see the momentum, and watch them come back to fill more orders 'til they've had their fill. This perhaps should be the first thing that anybody ever reads regarding trading: We're always looking for signs of what the big guys are doing at significant areas, and if we don't see what they're doing, there's no trade. So, on approach, if we see the big guys trying to hide their orders in the market, we see compression, and can feel pretty sure of their intentions - to get in as many orders as they can before the turn If we don't see this, we can be pretty sure that it won't just turn immediately, as there usually won't be enough orders against them to fill all the orders they must fill. This is why we wait for an engulf. This shows their intention to reverse price. Then we watch them trying to hide their orders in the market on a retrace, ready to take price to the origin of the move. When we see decent CP coming into the base of a pole, we are very often safe to touch trade the base. The safest thing to do however is to await the first engulf into the cp zone as confirmation. Very often a zone will break strongly and price will retrace but fail to retouch it. This is still the FTR - the confirmation of a new trend (do a study of how price reacts and how far it goes after hitting this spot). So an FTR can be first time back, but doesn't need to be. During holidays, volume in the market is often greatly diminished. This would lead some to imagine that price hardly moves. But. Say someone decided to put a truckload of orders into the market. If there's nobody else in the market to oppose these orders, price can do nothing but shoot away. So remember. Low Volume can = High Volatility . Until now I have been so unfocused on the charts that my exits have been very sloppy. My trade plan now has a couple of variables, but essentially I'll let price travel back to the other edge of the last PAZ in the TF I'm trading. If it engulfs, I'll exit on a RT or a break of the next LTF FL. If it rejects, I'll let the trade run and await exit PA. It's all about getting into the mind of the market makers and trading as they do. Nothing special. Most of my analysis comes in after the trade is entered. Before taking the trade, I do as you said - simple - it's really easy to find pockets of orders which will bounce price, and if they happen to be at great htf levels, even better - there's the highest chance of them giving maximum pips. What I do certainly looks like touch trading - picking tops and bottoms, but what you said belies that. These are not tops and bottoms, but retraces to the best price to re enter. Once I'm in though, I'm never guaranteed massive returns - sure price will bounce where I enter, but I'm never complacent until I've seen the engulf. In fact, I'm never really complacent at all. If PA tells me to get out, I must get out! Many might misconstrue us as pattern recognition traders - we're not. Certainly while learning we look for recurring patterns in the market. But once we understand them, what becomes most important is WHY the ITs made them. It's paramount to understand that it's not enough for the ITs to simply move price. They must also get massive amounts of orders filled in order to make maximum gains. They must also refrain from giving other ITs false signals, which could ultimately cause chaos for everybody. Think of these things as you study, and you'll be able to get into the mind of the market mover. Here are just a few targets for price, and the QM level is a big one. Certainly we need to get PA for entry before or once it's hit. If it breaks, then the same level can have the opposite effect on return. Once price engulfs a level, all that's important is how far it retraces before hitting its target. While the pockets of orders remain in this RT, it remains strong. If price totally compresses (picking up all orders) forward from the tip of the RT, then we will look primarily for the orders at the entrance to said CP. To the ITs, candle closes don't mean a damned thing, so please don't use them in your own analysis. A line is not the answer. Certainly, you may draw a line, but you must then go into the LTF to find a DBR/RBD on the right side of the LL/HH swing which covers that line. That RBD/DBR will be your box. You can scalp from each of these, knowing that it may only be a scalp. If you're simply setting a PO, then you must set your stop beyond the FL the HH/LL is a reaction to. The usable engulf is the one which hasn't hit its target. Every engulf has a very specific target. Apply that statement to your charts and eventually you'll see what I mean. Being only a sporadic trader (I really couldn't sit and watch the charts all day anymore!), I tend to open the charts from time to time and ask myself what's coming up in the next few minutes for me to take. If I'm lucky, I'll open the charts when we're at an HTF level. If not, I'll gladly take whatever high R M1 or whatever is there for the picking. 30 pips with a 3 pip stop is exactly the same as 150 pips with a 15. If there's nothing decent to take, I shut the charts. If I were asked where to trade, in one word, I'd say: Stops I'm way too disorganised to use limit orders! I just open the charts from time to time, and if I see the ITs scaring the retailers into closing good trades at a good level, I enter. I'll take off some of the position at the first target, so if my stop gets taken I can profit overall, then watch PA level by level. If price doesn't get into a big zone quickly, I'll usually get bored and go flat, having made enough to cover my next week's expenses. If I were truly meticulous, I'd treat my exits the same as my entries, and trade up and down all day, but trading is usually way down on my to-do list. Certainly there's an awful lot to learn here. But if I were to summarise what I think is most important, I'd say look to an engulf into free space that hasn't yet hit the origin (tg). Very often it will retrace deeply before advancing to the origin. Learn to spot these, and you'll be better equipped than most other traders out there. Price moves from PAZ to PAZ. The clear target for any trade after an engulf is the other end of the PAZ in that TF. If you zoom out to HTFs, you may find the TG is even further, but if not, stick to the TF you're in. I just want to warn you though that watching candles is an absolute waste of time. It distracts you from reading the story of price. The chart is a page, and a candle is a word. A word in itself has little meaning; it can be taken out of context. Sure, a sentence can be very powerful, as can a group of candles. But to get a real sense of the story, we need to view it all as a whole - be aware of how this paragraph relates to one many chapters back, and get a sense of where the story will lead in the future. In essence, we know that if price engulfs South, it wants to move down to the last engulf North. We want to read the story of price, and believe me, price has a story! You'll need to go further left to get your analysis right. Yes, you've marked levels well, but what are those levels a reaction to? Without knowing this, you're just gambling. So, look left, read the story, and be better equipped to predict what'll come next. Ask yourself "Why did price shoot up from there?" You'll answer "Because someone wanted to buy a lorryload, but there was nobody willing to sell at that price, so price shot up to find sellers." The next question you'll ask yourself is "Will he have left orders to buy again at that price?" The answer is usually "yes". Next question is "will price reverse from there?" The answer is, "Well, it may well bounce form there, but we won't know if it'll reverse until an engulf tells us it's reversed" Of course, the extremes in one TF can be midrange in another TF, which is why it's vital to manage your adds in the lower TF until they break into HTF trades. Okay! One giant clue: If something which should have been important got ignored, then it will be given great import on return. Personally, I love to dissect the HTF zone, in LTF, and look for a DBR or RBD within it, where price had broken out of a box and failed to get back in. Whipsaw engulfing - a fakeout followed by a quick return breaking the last zone. It's great PA. An excellent Supply or Demand zone is one where the future has already been written. Having done some study of the markets, we know that once we have an engulf of a zone, price will want to go to the origin. So we look to where the trend change was confirmed - FTR. You must study the zone which is being reacted to just as much as the reaction itself. Just consider the manipulation of hope and fear at turning points, and you'll have a very valuable eureka moment. When you begin to see the symmetry in the market, you're making one of the final steps in reading and predicting it. High R is High R, and these trades happen with great frequency. I applaud this easy way of making good money. If you're at the MPL of an HTF level, however, think about taking enough at LTF tg1 to cover the HTF stop, and letting the trade run. A bit of simple advice, to avoid overtrading and impulse trading: Draw up the most important looking zones, and look for trades only there. We absolutely must have an hard stop, always. But if we don't have an engulf before entry, we don't put it directly above the high or below the low, where all the retail stops lie. Instead, we find a lovely LTF RBD/DBR just beyond, and put it on the other side of that, so that we have the best chance to get out at BE or in big profit from the usual RT. There's no indication that a demand has been respected until the source above has been engulfed. Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable.
