The issue you raised can be the difference between success and failure. I've just finished a webinar with the Academy. We discussed the same stuff we discuss in every webinar, yet the attendees still seemed to get a lot out of it. This means that for many, learning comes from repetition. Now, when we talk in the Academy, we can be talking about one topic, yet we remain mindful of all the other topics which have an influence on price. It can take years to be able to see it all at once. Some get it in a couple of months, sure, but for most it's a long journey. The Academy Lite is made to be different. Let's use a metaphor. We want to make a cup of tea. In the Academy, to do this, we teach about the electricity which powers the kettle, the specific heat capacity of water and metal, the bimetalic strip which turns off the kettle, the latent heat of vapourisation of water, how tea is grown, distributed, sold and stored, everything about milk, sugar, etc. In the Academy Lite, we'll teach how to fill a kettle, let it boil, throw a teabag into a cup, pour water and add milk and sugar to taste. Both can achieve exactly the same results. It's just that one gives a greater understanding of the process. So, for the beginning of the lesson, all charts will be hand drawn. But we'll then move on to real chart based examples. I've kept the drawing of levels as simple as possible, so that a trading system can easily be formed. This means that students will have more losses than the Academy students, sure, but our money management lesson will make sure that overall profits can easily be made. So, if you want to know the basics of how to make a perfect cup of tea, this is the place to go Disclaimer: We will not be teaching how to make tea, but let me say that Earl Gray with milk and two sugars is absolutely lovely Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. My apologies if I sound cynical Characteristics of Capitalism Throughout its history, but especially during its ascendency in the 19th century, capitalism has had certain key characteristics. First, basic production facilities—land and capital—are privately owned. Capital in this sense means the buildings, mach ines, and other equipment used to produce goods and services that are ultimately consumed. Second, economic activity is organized and coordinated through the interaction of buyers and sellers (or producers) in markets. Third, owners of land and capit al as well as the workers they employ are free to pursue their own self-interests in seeking maximum gain from the use of their resources and labor in production. Consumers are free to spend their incomes in ways that they believe will yield the grea test satisfaction. This principle, called consumer sovereignty, reflects the idea that under capitalism producers will be forced by competition to use their resources in ways that will best satisfy the wants of consumers. Self-interest and the pursuit of gain lead them to do this. Fourth, under this system a minimum of government supervision is required; if competition is present, economic activity will be self- regulating. Government will be necessary only to protect society from foreign attack, uphold the rights of private property, and guarantee contracts. This 19th-century view of government’s role in the capitalist system has been significantly modified by ideas and events of the 20th century. Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. RBR/DBR are formations, as well as metaphors. These formations are what I see as canonical examples of something more subtle - disequilibrium. The base of DBR is the area of focus, for it has within it an area of equilibrium - the base. Price bounces tightly in a state of balance, and then eventually price rises, fast or slow. The way in which price leaves an area is what the focus is in the end as far as I see it - if price leaves slowly, the probability of orders being left at the base area is lower than if price shoots away. In IF's diagram the base is at the bottom of the PAZ. That is a DBR for sure, and the R piece engulfs the upper supply. The source of this move then is the move away from the base. But notice also that price pulls back and makes an FTR, which itself is a variant of a DBR. Again, when price leaves the FTR, if it moves well, it becomes an area of significance when price revisits. When price is seemingly stable, and then moves quickly away, this is place to focus on. It is the Balance->Imbalance cycle. You can spot this all over a chart. A good example is at the extremes. Imagine price breaking to new highs, and then struggle to get higher. Then a ledge is formed as price falls - a type of base with perhaps the highs falling but the lows remaining at the same level for 5 bars or so. Then price plummets, confirming supply is up here - this is one version of what some refer to as a hook. The point being that price might not look like a canonical base, RBR, DBR, RBD, etc....the key is to look beyond that, IMHO. HTH, MF. Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 31 Dec 2016 02:37 #2315 jsr --> Offline Trader Posts: 30 Thank you received: 42 This video is for those who think that struggling is a sign that you can't do this, As someone implied, all what we need is a simple shift in our mindset. These are some nuggets: So how do we learn? And why does some of us learn things more easily than others? every time you learn a new fact or skill, you change your brain. It's something we call neuroplasticity. So your brain can change in three very basic ways to support learning: So neuroplasticity is supported by chemical, by structural, and by functional changes, and these are happening across the whole brain. They can occur in isolation from one or another, but most often, they take place in concert. Together, they support learning. And they're taking place all the time. all of our behaviors change our brain. these changes are not limited by age, The primary driver of change in your brain is your behavior, so there is no neuroplasticity drug you can take. Nothing is more effective than practice at helping you learn, and the bottom line is you have to do the work. And in fact, my research has shown increased difficulty, increased struggle if you will, during practice, actually leads to both more learning, and greater structural change in the brain. You've had the experience of getting better and better within a single session of practice, and thinking "I have got it." And then, maybe you return the next day, and all those improvements from the day before are lost. What happened? Well, in the short term, your brain was able to increase the chemical signaling between your neurons. But for some reason, those changes did not induce the structural changes that are necessary to support long term memory. Remember that long term memories take time. And what you see in the short term does not reflect learning, It's these physical changes that are now going to support ong term memories, and chemical changes that support short term memories. The uniqueness of your brain will affect you both as a learner and also as a teacher. This idea helps us to understand why some children can thrive in tradition ducation settings and others don't; why some of us can learn languages easily and yet, others can pick up any sport and excel. So when you leave this room today, your brain will not be the same as when you entered this morning. And I think that's pretty amazing. But each of you is going to have changed your brain differently. Understanding these differences, these individual patterns, these variability and change is going to enable the next great advance in neuroscience; it's going to allow us to develop new and more effective interventions, and allow for matches between learners and teachers, and patients and interventions. And this does not just apply the recovery from stroke, it applies to each of us, as a parent, as a teacher, as a manager, and also because you are at TEDx today, as a lifelong learner. Study how and what you learn best. Repeat those behaviors that are healthy for your brain, and break those behaviors and habits that are not. Practice. Learning is about doing the work that your brain requires. So the best strategies are going to vary between individuals. You know what, they're even going to vary within individuals. So for you, learning music may come very easily, but learning to snowboard, much harder. Understand that everything you do, everything you encounter, and everything you experience is changing your brain. And that can be for better, but it can also be for worse. So when you leave today, go out and build the brain you want. Happy 2017! Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. In this case TG (UFL) has been hit. Therefore, the green box (LFL) is now an confirmed FL. The engulf downward is not significant. It is just part of retracement in the creation of the LFL (green box). The LFL (green box) is just the left shoulder, assuming that price does not break above the UFL and decides to come down and engulf the green box. So, we now have to wait for price to come down from the TG (UFL) and engulf the LFL (green box) for PA. Otherwise, if price continues going up and break above the UFL, the green box is just another LFL. Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 16 Feb 2017 17:08 #2406 Atari --> Offline Associate Trader Posts: 146 Thank you received: 389 Staurum, try to make it simple. For example, think about FL as a retracement in price. How do you know when that retracement is over? Answer, it is over when price hits the next FL to its left. That is where orders are left waiting there to be filled (in the next FL). After it hits the FL to its left (where orders are left waiting to be filled), then you can say, the retracement (FL) is confirmed and we can now draw a box around it. And we only look for FLs that are significant. The significant ones are the ones that engulfed a FL to its left. Otherwise it is not important. Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. ( IF ) Posts: 268 Thank you received: 573 Hi Guys. Just back from a business trip, trying to recap your posts. During these days I thought about our discussion here and I think I could risk to overcomplicate and over analyzing things. So I thought I share here my latest considerations, of course ready to accept any comment and/or different point of view. Actually what we learn overall in this great forum is to read Price Action, and take advantage from that Edge. And what is Price Action ? Or a Price Action Zone ? It is Price moving in a way to "prepare" a later decision. For this reason Price Action is what happens between two DP. In a CP PAZ, for example, Price can decide to go back and fill it or shoot in the opposite direction. Also in this case the two extremes of this zone will be important on return. At those points Price will either bounce or show a new Decision: EG The Engulf tells us that Price violated "Structure" and changed "Trend" until the next Structure level to be retested. The next DP It is like Trend Structure. Bullish, Bearish or Sideway. A trend is not anymore such, as soon as its structure gets violated. A PAZ is completed as soon as it achieves its next Limit (DP or FL) and confirms or negate the move to the next one. That's my "Thinking about Price". And Clouds are getting sharper to a clear Image. So based on this I would think the following statements may be correct about BSZ: - More frequent than the trades based on EG PA - Tend to have less R than trades based on EG PA and; - The win rate may be slightly lower than trades based on EG PA Only my two cents. The following user(s) said Thank You: cuimingzhao Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You Will it be this? 16 Mar 2017 18:11 #2475 Atari --> Offline Associate Trader Posts: 146 Thank you received: 389 HCDE, I recall IF answering another student about the same question you had on "I have a very very hard time finding space, engulf not hitting its target.". Yes, we need to find space otherwise, there is no trade. If it was easy to find space, then everyone would become a successful trader overnight. The ITs will not make it easy and obvious. Trading is based on your preference and your comfort zone and your confidence in your analysis. There are master traders who take touch trades and take confirmation trade. It all depends on the trade itself. First, I would suggest you get comfortable with confirmation trades before jumping to touch trade. Confirmation trades will provide you more winners and put money in the bank for you. It will also build your confidence. Touch trading can be tricky, so you need to read the market correctly.... . You need to know if the level it is reacting to is the true supply..... you need to know how it reacted when it reached that level....., for example did price impulsive move away from that level and engulf an important FL to its left without hitting TG. If so, you have PA.. Now you want to see how price is retracing and approaching your entry point.(in this example, I am describing a QM)...... is it compressing, is it compressing and then a final impulsive move to your entry level....These are the questions that you need to answer. The 1/2 page on article on price reading in Marketpedia speaks it all. So, I would recommend you reading it over and over again until you truly understand. If you have any question, then you can post them and other students will help answer. Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU If #232 Hotochin Offline Trader Posts: 588 Thank you received: 749 Jam, I don't think IF will mind if I answer some of your questions. I was actually talking about this with someone else one this forum. Think of FTR's as the flag limits. I have attached a chart with engulfs and the following flag limits marked with purple arrows. Notice how price "stair steps its way up?" When one of the limits gets engulfed that is your clue as to where price wants to go! When a whole zone gets engulfed you will be amazed at how price will respect them on the way down. Notice how price is compressed while in the zones? I think the trick is to watch the extremes of these zones and look for PA on smaller time frames for confirmation. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=225 9/31 7/27/2018 If - Page 10 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Good luck, H Attachments: The following user(s) said Thank You: Les_Paul, Jambowlyai This shall be the beginning of an end to a very long journey for me. Yes, we need to find space otherwise, there is no trade. If it was easy to find space, then everyone would become a successful trader overnight. The ITs will not make it easy and obvious. Trading is based on your preference and your comfort zone and your confidence in your analysis. There are master traders who take touch trades and take confirmation trade. It all depends on the trade itself. First, I would suggest you get comfortable with confirmation trades before jumping to touch trade. Confirmation trades will provide you more winners and put money in the bank for you. It will also build your confidence. Touch trading can be tricky, so you need to read the market correctly.... . You need to know if the level it is reacting to is the true supply..... you need to know how it reacted when it reached that level....., for example did price impulsive move away from that level and engulf an important FL to its left without hitting TG. If so, you have PA.. Now you want to see how price is retracing and approaching your entry point.(in this example, I am describing a QM)...... is it compressing, is it compressing and then a final impulsive move to your entry level....These are the questions that you need to answer. The 1/2 page on article on price reading in Marketpedia speaks it all. So, I would recommend you reading it over and over again until you truly understand. I see the symmetry as floors of a building where the price goes from one to another. Imagine that the price is a ball. A ball may bounce upward on the floor or down on the ceiling of a floor. But this ball also has the ability to cross the floor or ceiling if given circumstances. The rule is that the ball will only bounce (if it does) on the floor or ceiling of the floor where it is at the moment (not in the space between them wich is the floor itself), and if it crosses for example the ceiling and goes upstairs, the inertia will take it to the roof of that new floor (target). Then it could bounce there or cross that roof at first touch and move to the next floor. That is, if the price comes from below, the ceiling of new floor to which it accedes will be the target Let's see the chart: https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=2650 3/34 7/27/2018 If - Page 107 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT The price (ball) reaches the roof of the first floor and does not bounce, it crosses. We have left the first floor behind and we are already on the second floor. What happens here? The price begins to rebound on the roof and the floor several times until finally it crosses the ceiling and goes to the third floor. The price has already left the second floor and will not be able to cross it back until it reaches the roof of the third floor (target).What do we have on the second floor? A FLAG. Which are its limits? The floor and ceiling of the second floor. Floors and ceilings are FLs and can be FTRs, S/R, etc, too. I supose that at he left the ceilings and floors are respected, too. What happens on the third floor? Reaches the ceiling and directly crosses (line 3) to the fourth floor, so it must go to the ceilong of that new floor (target). What happens on the fourth floor? The ball (price) bounces a couple of times on ceiling and floor and crosses the floor returning to the floor below (third floor). As I said before, the price can only bounce off the floor and ceiling. As it comes from the ceiling, where could it bounce? On the floor, which is in turn the second floor ceiling. And so on. So what conclusion can we draw from this symmetry? The price will always bounce off the ceiling or floor and not anywhere else inside the floor. Therefore, WE ONLY MUST PLAN THE TRADES AT FLOOR OR CEILING OF THE FLOOR IN WHICH WE FIND US. OR WHAT IS THE SAME, IN THE FLs, FTR, etc. The engulf of one floor with a Flag inside will shoe us intentions to continue in the direction of the engulf. In the future, this structure of floors will be respected and the importance of each floor depend on what you have in the past on that floor PD: It is possible that everything I have said is nothing but nonsense. But the market is moved by people. Most of these people we see over and over again, making plays from the same book all week long. Sometimes though, a new player will dump a ton of orders into the market; more than the ITs are willing to cover, and a level will break. Sometimes an IT will himself make a slip and accidentally break a level. Sometimes an IT will break a level just to mess with us lot's brains. These events are extremely rare, but they do happen. If they didn't happen, we could go all in on every trade, and soon find ourselves as rich as the Rothschilds! It's due to this risk of false PA that we only risk a small percent of our accounts on any trade or set of correlated trades. Note: Should the ITs ever change their rulebook, don't worry. To answer a PM I got, which was "Is there any way to know how far will the retrace will happen after the break of the level?" No.It can retrace to any set of clean orders in the zone it's traveled through. Ideally it will travel all the way back for a QM at the MPL, or even break the H/L for a DM, but it often only retraces a short way, leaving the clean orders beyond for later. At each minor level it retraces to, we can take confirmed LTF trades, taking some profits to cover losses, letting some run to the HTF target, should this be the depth of the RT https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=2700 22/32 7/27/2018 If - Page 109 - RTM Community The following user(s) said Thank You: ashiki, hndrk, HCDE, linos, alirezat, Frosty, Shantala, HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Andrey7, cuimingzhao, dengaima With time, patience and experience, what once seemed very complex becomes very simple indeed Please join www.theblue.community QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU If #2721 bobyv87 Offline Associate Trader Posts: 330 Thank you received: 316 So, does that means that you can't touch trade at the very MPL at each minor level but instead we only look for confirmed LTF trades? The big spikes that happen right before and during a news release are rarely caused by ITs dropping massive orders and then reversing their orders with even more massive orders the other way. What often happens is that some IT's (since ITs trade different time frames too) remove their orders from the market. This causes a vacuum of orderflow where price moves to find new equilibrium. When we are talking about a spike to supply, there was more demand than supply once IT pulled their orders. This allows the sharp move higher to strong supply or an area with lots of retail buy stops (because IT takes opposite of retail). Then price falls because of overwhelming supply. I tried many times to spot engulfs into a FL (opposed to engulf of a FL). But when doing that i was considering in the same way a break in between two targets Inside the FL than a break in between the S/R kink of the FL and the first iLS. This is a mistake, because by breaking S/R kink and reaching first iLS, price reaches it's TG and therefore validates a new UFL Any break of that UFL is actually PA UP... So in that situation we shouldn't expect price to retrace to the UFL we came from and then get further into the LFL... Lesson learned. So either die at the enemy shore or defeat the 1000 men and take over and live. Flamed? Not at all! I'm delighted this came up in such a polite and considerate manner :) The article doesn't need editing at all. RTM has the most comprehensive and no BS Wiki course on trading that has ever been written, and it's all on the site for free! The paid course is a luxury rather than a necessity. Anybody who puts in the work to make the free lessons their own, has just as much chance of making it as those who pay for the course. The course is just a shortcut. No more, no less. It was implicit that the first rung of RTM was all about reading the market. Learning to trade it was to be a personal journey, aided by seniors as one climbs the ladder. But there'll be a module on the course dedicated to trading, and making trade plans to suit each lifestyle and personality. So yes, in this case, there IS a difference. It may seem that I started RTM for altruistic reasons, but that's not the case. Sure, I stop to help people who've broken down or are in some other trouble, but I do that because it makes ME feel good. I started RTM to make an army of great traders who'll work with me in the future. No altruism there. I'm delighted I did, as we already have our first fund traders lined up and ready to go. So why don't I now hand out ALL I know for free to everybody? I steal orders from the big institutions, but not so many that they lose out. It's a long and sometimes lonely road we must walk. He admits he's still not got it, and gave me a list of his ideas for my advice This is good stuff, and I want to share it If you would be kind enough to advise me if I am at least close to the Golden Egg it would be appreciated. 1: There is no such system that is a "Holy Grail" ...full stop. Wrong! The market is run by people who know what they're doing. They use a finite number of tools to trick retailers into offering orders up to them. They use a finite number of algorithms to do their work for them. In this post you were asked what is the difference between an engulf and a fake out. No answer was provided. I understand that an engulf involves price making a lower low on reaction to Supply, or higher high on reaction to Demand. More importantly, it shows intent of price to continue in the direction of the engulf. I also understand that a fake out occurs in order to find sufficient liquidity to sell/buy against. More importantly, it is followed by a change in direction. Knowing if the break of "A" is an engulf or fake out requires analysis of the complete picture (higher time frames and looking left). Thanks, d Hi Buddy, "I understand that an engulf involves price making a lower low on reaction to Supply, or higher high on reaction to Demand" - This can be correct, but it certainly is not always correct, actually most of the time it isn't correct. You need to find the important engulfs of flags, it is when these happen that an engulf becomes meaningful. Simply making a higher high or lower low will not show you any intent. Also understand that an engulf will achieve the same thing as a FO (in terms of retailer trading behaviour) but it is the signal that price wants to go to the next important level in the direction of the engulf. A FO is simply a ploy to trap traders once the signal engulf has already happened. Study up on flag limits, there has been some very good posting on them recently, understanding the FL and the engulfs of the FL's along with a HTF analysis and you will be able to tell the FO from the Engulf. On the topic for tonight's management meeting is why I haven't resolved it yet, so I'd better get in here and answer it before I get a rollicking :) So let's get to it: https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=625 21/42 7/27/2018 If - Page 26 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT 1. The leading IT engulfed price back up into the range (engulfed V), showing he was taking price up to the last FL above (U) 2. The other ITs, who had been short from high above, saw that price had turned, and wanted out of their shorts and into long positions. So they sold against the retail breakout long trades They will have Faked Out below a ltf demand (not visible in this tf), scaring the BO buyers into selling at a loss, and enticing BO sellers, giving them lots to buy against and go net long. 3. A marker was set for future use 4. They turned price before the target, creating a supply which could be broken later 5. Price had been dropping for some time, attracting lots of retail sellers; the IT's were eating these up bit by bit. It was obvious to the more savvy of the retailers that price was heading for W. So the natural thing to do was turn price before the tg, creating a demand to be faked later. They buy heavily, taking all the herd's sells and shooting price back up. 6. They removed their pending orders at 4, allowing price to break supply. All the short retailers freak out and start closing by buying. This allows the ITs to sell to them, beginning the process of going from long to short. 7. They begin to flag price downwards, adding little shorts as they create LLs and LHs. Now when it comes to levels and stops, I was always under the belief that if a new level was created during active market hours within your zone, then that becomes your new trade/ risk area. A little unwritten rule of thumb that I have myself is that at least a new 1hr, 30 min, or 15 min embedded zone has to be created for me to make that my NEW trade/ risk area upon revisit since higher TFs are more reliable. Here is an example of a trade I took yesterday on the CADCHF. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=900 24/40 7/27/2018 If - Page 37 - RTM Community 1hr HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT 4hr As you can see, the trade I took was a plane jane trade that was simply based off of the 4hr zone that cause the consumption of upper supply. Since we were still clearly in an uptrend with a plausible 4hr target overhead yet to be hit, I figured I would go for it even though we didn't get the full engulf. The trade worked out fine, but in the LTFs, I watched the action develop, and a setup that I have always considered valid came up. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=900 25/40 7/27/2018 If - Page 37 - RTM Community Here is the setup I'm talking about as previously mentioned in the first two paragraphs, HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT 1hr As you can see, there was a new 1hr demand zone that was created WITHIN my 4hr zone during the active market hours. In my mind, this was a high probability trade which I would have probably taken on the retest if I wasn't already in the trade. My logic for this is if a NEW 1hr demand zone was created when pro money was active, then why have my stop beyond the original 4hr zone? Whey not enter on the retrace to the newly created 1hr demand and have your stop below that? That is the same logic I had in my EURGBP trade, so assuming we did get the proper PA and engulfed the 1min FO level, why would my stop still need to be below the original zone you showed since this would have been a NEW 1hr demand zone within the 4hr demand?? The way I have always looked at it, playing PA to the right like this increases RR and I have seen it work a hundred times before in my studies. As for the TP, it would have stayed the same for me (the 'ultimate profit target' in the 4hr chart) since this was a new 30 min or greater embedded demand zone. If this were just a newly created 15 min demand zone, I would have switched to 'intraday' mode and my ultimate TP would have been more conservatively based upon the lower 4hr zone that caused the retrace. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=900 26/40 7/27/2018 If - Page 37 - RTM Community Also, with regard to PA, I personally have a problem with zooming all the way down to HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT the 1min to check for the limits to be engulfed because when you get down that low, it seems you can always make a case (or a least most times) as to whey 'this' or 'that' 1min zone is the reason price is being held down. It can just get very messy, confusing, and paralyzing when you go down that low to look for confirmation because there are rarely places in the chart where one will have a complete liquidity gap/ pole down to the 1 min. If I were to scrutinize every trade I took to this level, well, I don't think I would ever take a trade because this is a perfect setup and the market rarely provides those in my eyes, which is why we have stops in the first place. Sorry for these long drawn out questions, but I feel these are key issues I have been battling with for a while now without avail. The only thing is, I am not affirmative of it yet. I would really appreciate it if you could help clear it up for me or comment on my thinking ! This is what I think --- 1. Use the s/d, s/r flip, ftr, etc. to identify the potential and high probability price reversal regions in a HTF. 2. As price returns to these identified zones, we switch to a LTF to see how price reacts. In the selected LTF, after price trades to the zone from Step 1, we wait for price to go back down or up to engulf a significant demand or supply formed before price reached the zone, or use the various other reaction price patterns discussed to confirm IT's intention of taking price down or up. 3. Then, as price returns to a supply or demand formed at or near the zone identified in Step 1, a touch trade or confirmed trade can be taken. 4. Place the stop beyond the edge of the zone identified in Step 1; target 1 is the next demand or supply in the LTF used, while the final target is the original of the move to the zone identified in Step 1, often the next demand or supply in that HTF used. The reason you wanted us to put the puzzle pieces together instead of handing over the golden keys is for us to accumulate the chart experiences (screen hours), and figure out what HTF and LTF would work, and to form the psychology to follow the plan. Many many thanks! J9 QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=1150 11/32 7/27/2018 If - Page 47 - RTM Community If EDUCATION FORUM MORE #1157 HOME LOGOUT geejay Offline Trader PRICE ACTION WILL SHOW YOU THE WAY Posts: 41 Thank you received: 63 Hi J9, Sure. At point 1 on the down side, we have an engulf. The little flag on the left side is a decision, a decision to go higher and go back into the M15 flag. On the way down, when this level marked by the red line in broken, we can say the demand was engulfed. Next price flags. It bottoms, reverses back to the red line, then on the next wave down, it makes a lower low. To me, that is a clear signal that price wants to go lower. So, when price comes back to 3, to test the cap at 1, it is a good place to go short. And a point to clarify about QM. They do work in all timeframes, M1 up to MON1. What I was referring to is their respective locations. We are more interested in QM that form in historical S and D zones. So, the way you marked up your QM, was for a short. But I don't see any Supply zone there. There is supply for sure but the way I learned QM was to expect them at higher TF supply zones (Daily Supply for example for shorts). Perhaps the easiest is to go back to the QM article and read it again as that is probably clearer than my explanation. GJ. The more I look at the charts the more I think big money is lazy and that is why this is so simple, I imagine big money goes like this, 'If price is above X then it is worth Y, when it gets to Y I'll make a decision, If Y is to expensive it is worth X, If Y is still to cheap, it is worth Z but no less than X'. And because big money is so lazy, these perceived levels of value are pretty evenly spaced, probably to the pip if we really wanted to take the time to find out. Well, I've found that such complexity can be intimidating, and can actually paralyse the student into not being able to understand any of it for some time. So, what I'll do this time is, at the very start of the course, teach the students how to make profits without knowing all the minutiae of the market. Easy setups which will pay nearly every time they're taken. I feel that if the students are making easy profits from the start, then the pressure to learn the finer points will be greatly reduced, allowing them to digest it faster. If their understanding of the market lies in the bottom dome of a sand-timer, the worst thing they can do is try to press it down from the top. That just causes a blockage at the neck. With the new method, they will hardly be paying attention to the timer at all, letting the sands fall as freely as they should. Probably I overthink .. as always There are 8 main currencies in the Forex market. It is possible to calculate currency indexes for each one - but it's not a straight average across each currency's crosspairs. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=1650 2/32 7/27/2018 If - Page 67 - RTM Community Instead, the trade figures for each currency are used, and the 5 most heavily traded HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT opposing currencies are used for the index weighting calculation. For example, this is JPYX: From these figures, you can calculate a correctly balanced currency index for each currency. I have had these for some time now, I coded them up in MT4 (AUDX/CADX/CHFX/EURX/GBPX/JPYX/NZDX/USDX). When correctly balanced, RTM style setups work exactly the same on these composite charts - except it is an entire currency that is making a move. Institutional money tends to flow from one currency into another, they don't adopt a view on a single pair. For the best trades, you find separate currencies forming opposing setups - when 2 currencies are moving in opposite directions, the relevant crosspair totally flies. Some brokers carry USDX and EURX, but the balancings are usually incorrect or out of date. You can also find things like GBPX online on some websites, but the calculation is a straight average across all crosses. This is nonsense really, to attach the same weighting to GBPNZD as EURGBP when forming a GBPX index. When used correctly, these are a massive odds enhancer. You get double confluence by checking the 2 indexes for each cross, to see if it supports your trade. It keeps me out of a lot of bad decisions. It also helps keep you on the right side of the market if you always try to play strongest vs weakest. There's a good article here on ForexFactory about it www.forexfactory.com/showthread.php?t=334165 In answer to your AUD question - if AUD is strong on the day, but JPY is stronger, the other AUD pairs will move up, but AJ will chop around at its short zone. If JPY remains strong as AUD hits supply, then it will drop. You quite often see this, one of the crosspairs "hanging around" at supply or demand, waiting for the index to hit the appropriate level before it moves off. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=1650 3/32 7/27/2018 If - Page 67 - RTM Community Here are the 8 currency indexes from today: HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT i.imgur.com/2JiLOeN.png Attachments: The following user(s) said Thank You: Mike1, freshtan, Rdk123, Whenever, dudu112, Art, Enlightenme, salivan, alirezat, cuimingzhao QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU If #1652 Ifmyante Offline Chief Cook and Bottle Washer If you see a piece of truth glistening in the dirt, get down on your knees and gently dig it out, for it's the greatest treasure you will ever find Posts: 3576 Thank you received: 14517 Now I'm dizzy https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=1650 4/32 7/27/2018 If - Page 67 - RTM Community Delighted to see such clever information here HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT The following user(s) said Thank You: cuimingzhao With time, patience and experience, what once seemed very complex becomes very simple indeed Please join www.theblue.community QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU If #1653 Rdk123 Offline Trader Posts: 282 Thank you received: 288 Mate, that was awesome, thank you for that, I'll be reading it a few more times. Taking LTF trend continuations on pullbacks to FLs, based on the bigger picture strongest vs weakest currencies, as inferred from the indexes, is the highest probability way to make easy pips, or even better, getting in right at the top of the whole currency turn (although picking tops/bottoms is always going to be riskier somewhat). Where a lot of currency strength indis fail, and we can do better with them, is that in order to determine a currency's strength, they use some sort of moving average to determine the trend - simply "is it going up right now, or going down right now?" We however, with our knowledge of PA, could look at EURX and say "well, it's going up right now, but we've had a significant engulf south, and now we've pulled back to a QM level, so in fact I don't think it's strong, I think it's about to become very weak". ShadowPit wrote: bobyv - I think you need to upload the chart with your additional markups to make sense of what you're asking The short answer to your question is Demand exceeded Supply at a level you have not drawn. My observations in black. Some general feedback using the chart for illustration: Be cautious with creating too higher expectation from one engulf or one observation you make. Trading requires consideration of multiple sources of information which may come from other time frames as well. Be careful not to expect price to make higher highs or lower lows, just because you identified an engulf of a level (note obstacle 1 & 2). Pay special attention to the QM level drawn on the chart, the level is more than a singular horizontal line, if you want to use just a single line, draw it under the lows of the "1" and "2". https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=1725 30/34 7/27/2018 If - Page 70 - RTM Community The QM level held price up on 4 occasions! On the 2nd, 3rd and 4th occasion it made a HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT higher high on this timeframe. There was no engulf of this zone, therefore you cannot rely on your expectation that price would go any lower than this zone at any stage of your analysis. In fact if you look on from point "4" the simple observation that no supply was holding price down and new demand was being created would tell you that a sell off was highly unlikely. Also last but not least, let's just say you did enter a touch trade short based on your assertion that price engulfed the low you have identified, you have obstacle #1 immediately below you, reducing your probability of success. Hope this helps. EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT HOME Attachments: QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU My Decision for gbp/jpy from h4 Chart #1755 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=1750 5/28 7/27/2018 If - Page 71 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT ShadowPit Offline Associate Trader Posts: 277 Thank you received: 1195 boby, First: To me A&C have nuanced differences: C is a clean looking DBR, it sits above a key level (resistance becomes support), it isn't compressed, it moves cleanly away AFTER the break of a key level (strong imbalance). A doesn't have the same characteristics, it is a compressed move, it doesn't sit on top of a key level, it sits underneath a recent high, it is BEFORE the break of a key level, it does however have an ok move out of the level which eventually runs into the HTF supply extremes without retracement to a demand level, which C does not have this characteristic. Onto the move up: B is the supply (DBD) that caused the break of C (DEMAND) which sits at a key level. C could have just as easily bounced price back up, but it didn't. D does not have this same characteristic, it breaks nothing of significance, it only extends the move lower into demand, and is very promptly broken. Having said that, strong imbalance of price is implied at both B and D until price tells us otherwise and you cannot presume that price will break either until it does. In this case, D is broken without any retracement so we look to B if it can hold price down, but it doesn't, which can only mean price has paved the way for higher prices. As buyers flood the market, sellers are either trapped and wanting to get out as close to their failed entries (at B and D) as possible or face being stopped out. (this is the psychological makeup of the market) Price will now look higher to find better supply, price will go higher from most RECENT _fresh_ demand if it can, which happened to fall at the break of D (remember the imbalance has now been flipped). This is the origin. Remember, the break of D is the source of breaking D AND B, surely a stronger https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=1750 6/28 7/27/2018 If - Page 71 - RTM Community imbalance of price compared to if it was only the source of breaking D and NOT B.. HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Even better is that this origin is in CONFLUENCE with the original KEY LEVEL (C) which is textbook perfect S/R which is where you always want to be placing your trades. Hope this helps. The issue you raised can be the difference between success and failure. I've just finished a webinar with the Academy. We discussed the same stuff we discuss in every webinar, yet the attendees still seemed to get a lot out of it. This means that for many, learning comes from repetition. Now, when we talk in the Academy, we can be talking about one topic, yet we remain mindful of all the other topics which have an influence on price. It can take years to be able to see it all at once. Some get it in a couple of months, sure, but for most it's a long journey. The Academy Lite is made to be different. Let's use a metaphor. We want to make a cup of tea. In the Academy, to do this, we teach about the electricity which powers the kettle, the specific heat capacity of water and metal, the bimetalic strip which turns off the kettle, the latent heat of vapourisation of water, how tea is grown, distributed, sold and stored, everything about milk, sugar, etc. In the Academy Lite, we'll teach how to fill a kettle, let it boil, throw a teabag into a cup, pour water and add milk and sugar to taste. Both can achieve exactly the same results. It's just that one gives a greater understanding of the process. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=2075 2/24 7/27/2018 If - Page 84 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT So, for the beginning of the lesson, all charts will be hand drawn. But we'll then move on to real chart based examples. I've kept the drawing of levels as simple as possible, so that a trading system can easily be formed. This means that students will have more losses than the Academy students, sure, but our money management lesson will make sure that overall profits can easily be made. So, if you want to know the basics of how to make a perfect cup of tea, this is the place to go Disclaimer: We will not be teaching how to make tea, but let me say that Earl Gray with milk and two sugars is absolutely lovely The following user(s) said Thank You: hndrk, staurum With time, patience and experience, what once seemed very complex becomes very simple indeed Please join www.theblue.community QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU If #2077 MarkN Offline Trader Posts: 7 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=2075 3/24 7/27/2018 If - Page 84 - RTM Community Thank you received: 13 HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT That's an excellent analogy! My apologies if I sound cynical Characteristics of Capitalism Throughout its history, but especially during its ascendency in the 19th century, capitalism has had certain key characteristics. First, basic production facilities--land and capital--are privately owned. Capital in this sense means the buildings, mach ines, and other equipment used to produce goods and services that are ultimately consumed. Second, economic activity is organized and coordinated through the interaction of buyers and sellers (or producers) in markets. Third, owners of land and capit al as well as the workers they employ are free to pursue their own self-interests in seeking maximum gain from the use of their resources and labor in production. Consumers are free to spend their incomes in ways that they believe will yield the grea test satisfaction. This principle, called consumer sovereignty, reflects the idea that under capitalism producers will be forced by competition to use their resources in ways that will best satisfy the wants of consumers. Self-interest and the pursuit of gain lead them to do this. Fourth, under this system a minimum of government supervision is required; if competition is present, economic activity will be self- regulating. Government will be necessary only to protect society from foreign attack, uphold the rights of private property, and guarantee contracts. This 19th-century view of government's role in the capitalist system has been significantly modified by ideas and events of the 20th century. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=2125 7/36 7/27/2018 If - Page 86 - RTM Community QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE FORUM MORE LOGOUT HOME EDUCATION THANK YOU If #2130 DeepBlue Offline Trader Posts: 23 Thank you received: 28 Ifmyante wrote: Why oh why do I argue with you? RBR/DBR are formations, as well as metaphors. These formations are what I see as canonical examples of something more subtle - disequilibrium. The base of DBR is the area of focus, for it has within it an area of equilibrium - the base. Price bounces tightly in a state of balance, and then eventually price rises, fast or slow. The way in which price leaves an area is what the focus is in the end as far as I see it - if price leaves slowly, the probability of orders being left at the base area is lower than if price shoots away. In IF's diagram the base is at the bottom of the PAZ. That is a DBR for sure, and the R piece engulfs the upper supply. The source of this move then is the move away from the base. But notice also that price pulls back and makes an FTR, which itself is a variant of a DBR. Again, when price leaves the FTR, if it moves well, it becomes an area of significance when price revisits. When price is seemingly stable, and then moves quickly away, this is place to focus on. It is the Balance->Imbalance cycle. You can spot this all over a chart. A good example is at the extremes. Imagine price breaking to new highs, and then struggle to get higher. Then a ledge is formed as price falls - a type of base with perhaps the highs falling but the lows remaining at the same level for 5 bars or so. Then price plummets, confirming supply is up here - this is one version of what some refer to as a hook. The point being that price might not look like a canonical base, RBR, DBR, RBD, etc....the key is to look https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=200 8/26 7/27/2018 If - Page 9 - RTM Community beyond that, IMHO. HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT HTH, MF. These are some nuggets: So how do we learn? And why does some of us learn things more easily than others? every time you learn a new fact or skill, you change your brain. It's something we call neuroplasticity. So your brain can change in three very basic ways to support learning: So neuroplasticity is supported by chemical, by structural, and by functional changes, and these are happening across the whole brain. They can occur in isolation from one or another, but most often, they take place in concert. Together, they support learning. And they're taking place all the time. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=2300 19/32 7/27/2018 If - Page 93 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT all of our behaviors change our brain. these changes are not limited by age, The primary driver of change in your brain is your behavior, so there is no neuroplasticity drug you can take. Nothing is more effective than practice at helping you learn, and the bottom line is you have to do the work. And in fact, my research has shown increased difficulty, increased struggle if you will, during practice, actually leads to both more learning, and greater structural change in the brain. You've had the experience of getting better and better within a single session of practice, and thinking "I have got it." And then, maybe you return the next day, and all those improvements from the day before are lost. What happened? Well, in the short term, your brain was able to increase the chemical signaling between your neurons. But for some reason, those changes did not induce the structural changes that are necessary to support long term memory. Remember that long term memories take time. And what you see in the short term does not reflect learning, It's these physical changes that are now going to support ong term memories, and chemical changes that support short term memories. The uniqueness of your brain will affect you both as a learner and also as a teacher. This idea helps us to understand why some children can thrive in tradition ducation settings and others don't; why some of us can learn languages easily and yet, others can pick up any sport and excel. So when you leave this room today, your brain will not be the same as when you entered this morning. And I think that's pretty amazing. But each of you is going to have changed your brain differently. Understanding these differences, these individual patterns, these variability and change is going to enable the next great advance in neuroscience; it's going to allow us to develop new and more https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=2300 20/32 7/27/2018 If - Page 93 - RTM Community effective interventions, and allow for matches between learners and teachers, HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT and patients and interventions. And this does not just apply the recovery from stroke, it applies to each of us, as a parent, as a teacher, as a manager, and also because you are at TEDx today, as a lifelong learner. Study how and what you learn best. Repeat those behaviors that are healthy for your brain, and break those behaviors and habits that are not. Practice. Learning is about doing the work that your brain requires. So the best strategies are going to vary between individuals. You know what, they're even going to vary within individuals. So for you, learning music may come very easily, but learning to snowboard, much harder. Understand that everything you do, everything you encounter, and everything you experience is changing your brain. And that can be for better, but it can also be for worse. So when you leave today, go out and build the brain you want. Happy 2017! QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU If #2406 Atari Offline RTM Moderator Posts: 172 Thank you received: 421 Staurum, try to make it simple. For example, think about FL as a retracement in price. How do you know when that retracement is over? Answer, it is over when price hits the next FL to its left. That is where orders are left waiting there to be filled (in the next FL). After it hits the FL to its left (where orders are left waiting to be filled), then you can say, the retracement (FL) is confirmed and we can now draw a box around it. And we only look for FLs that are significant. The significant ones are the ones that engulfed a FL to its left. Otherwise it is not important. HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Actually what we learn overall in this great forum is to read Price Action, and take advantage from that Edge. And what is Price Action ? Or a Price Action Zone ? It is Price moving in a way to "prepare" a later decision. For this reason Price Action is what happens between two DP. In a CP PAZ, for example, Price can decide to go back and fill it or shoot in the opposite direction. Also in this case the two extremes of this zone will be important on return. At those points Price will either bounce or show a new Decision: EG The Engulf tells us that Price violated "Structure" and changed "Trend" until the next Structure level to be retested. The next DP It is like Trend Structure. Bullish, Bearish or Sideway. A trend is not anymore such, as soon as its structure gets violated. A PAZ is completed as soon as it achieves its next Limit (DP or FL) and confirms or negate the move to the next one. That's my "Thinking about Price". And Clouds are getting sharper to a clear Image. I'm glad there's a lot of discussion in here, as I know where my journal is! I want to answer a question I get asked a lot: "In which timeframe do you trade?" There's no need to trade timeframes. Just trade high R instead, which could be on any scale. If price is at a nice weekly SR kink, which is only a few pips wide, or it's at the MPL of a larger kink, await M1 PA. If there's space in that TF to get >1R to the M1 approach kink, then take the trade, closing enough at tg1 to cover your stop, then allow price to either hit the weekly approach kink (watch PA there to see if you should close all or allow to run) or your https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=2425 6/30 7/27/2018 If - Page 98 - RTM Community stop. The following user(s) said Thank You: cuimingzhao QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Will it be this? #2475 Atari Offline RTM Moderator Posts: 172 Thank you received: 421 HCDE, I recall IF answering another student about the same question you had on "I have a very very hard time finding space, engulf not hitting its target.". Yes, we need to find space otherwise, there is no trade. If it was easy to find space, then everyone would become a successful trader overnight. The ITs will not make it easy and obvious. Trading is based on your preference and your comfort zone and your confidence in your analysis. There are master traders who take touch trades and take confirmation trade. It all depends on the trade itself. First, I would suggest you get comfortable with confirmation trades before jumping to touch trade. Confirmation trades will provide you more winners and put money in the bank for you. It will also build your confidence. Touch trading can be tricky, so you need to read the market correctly.... . You need to know if the level it is reacting to is the true supply..... you need to know how it reacted when it reached that level....., for example did price impulsive move away from that level and engulf an important FL to its left without hitting TG. If so, you have PA.. Now you want to see how price is retracing and approaching your entry point.(in this https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/1523-if?start=2450 32/34 7/27/2018 If - Page 99 - RTM Community example, I am describing a QM)...... is it compressing, is it compressing and then a final HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT impulsive move to your entry level....These are the questions that you need to answer. The 1/2 page on article on price reading in Marketpedia speaks it all. So, I would recommend you reading it over and over again until you truly understand. If you have any question, then you can post them and other students will help answer. I was actually talking about this with someone else one this forum. Think of FTR's as the flag limits. I have attached a chart with engulfs and the following flag limits marked with purple arrows. Notice how price "stair steps its way up?" When one of the limits gets engulfed that is your clue as to where price wants to go! When a whole zone gets engulfed you will be amazed at how price will respect them on the way down. Notice how price is compressed while in the zones? I think the trick is to watch the extremes of these zones and look for PA on smaller time frames for confirmation. Good luck, H Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Yes, we need to find space otherwise, there is no trade. If it was easy to find space, then everyone would become a successful trader overnight. The ITs will not make it easy and obvious. Trading is based on your preference and your comfort zone and your confidence in your analysis. There are master traders who take touch trades and take confirmation trade. It all depends on the trade itself. First, I would suggest you get comfortable with confirmation trades before jumping to touch trade. Confirmation trades will provide you more winners and put money in the bank for you. It will also build your confidence. Touch trading can be tricky, so you need to read the market correctly.... . You need to know if the level it is reacting to is the true supply..... you need to know how it reacted when it reached that level....., for example did price impulsive move away from that level and engulf an important FL to its left without hitting TG. If so, you have PA.. Now you want to see how price is retracing and approaching your entry point.(in this example, I am describing a QM)...... is it compressing, is it compressing and then a final impulsive move to your entry level....These are the questions that you need to answer. The 1/2 page on article on price reading in Marketpedia speaks it all. So, I would recommend you reading it over and over again until you truly understand. If you have any question, then you can post them and other students will help answer. Thanks for your answer, it helps me. I end up having a good price reading skills, I think I got what are the mecanisms behind left shoulders, i understand why there is symetry in the market I understand the concepts and I think what is behind it. But I'm really psychologically challenged by these confirmation trades. I know myself, i'm cautious so I set myself a rule which is just take confirmation trade. But I find so few of them that I get very very psychologically challenged. To be honest, I expected a lot of QM on one pair on small timeframes... I think I'm gonna change the way I screen the market. I used to take one or two pairs at a time and focus on them all day long. I think that's not working for me. I'm gonna screen every pair I have every morning, asking myself: "Are we at a good HTF level or near that? If yes, monitor and wait for confirmation, if no, go on..." What about you guys, what is your trading routine? Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. If - Page 103 - RTM Community ReadTheMarket.com The only School which understands The Market Index Recent Topics New Topic No Replies My Topics Private Messages Preferences Welcome, indo-investasi Last login: Today 01:42 Forum Members' Journals Journals If Reply Topic Favorite Page: 1 ... 98 99 100 101 102 103 104 105 106 107 ... 139 TOPIC: If If 26 Apr 2017 20:37 #2551 Ifmyante Topic Author --> Offline Chief Cook and Bottle Washer If you see a piece of truth glistening in the dirt, get down on your knees and gently dig it out, for it's the greatest treasure you will ever find Posts: 3574 Thank you received: 14393 Okay so I got quite lost in that video! But let me respond to what I think I understood of it. If a FL is visible in a certain timeframe, then it is a FL on that TF. If it's the kink of the top or bottom of an higher TF FL, it becomes significant in the HTF. My definition of a BSZ differs from your video. For me, a BSZ is the area beyond two or more horizontally aligned highs/lows, set to trick retailers into believing the S/R is strong, and trading it with stops beyond. Even if his ask line tested your level, they can't break every level as they want. They still have to have approximately the same feed like the institutional broker. So, if in your insituttional broker data feed a level is holding price down i dont think the retailed broker will break that level by 100 pips. Sure, it could happen, but most of the time not. I think with a proper data feed you can be absolute certain that you have fresh orders inside a level or not and this can give you a massive edge. I see the symmetry as floors of a building where the price goes from one to another. Imagine that the price is a ball. A ball may bounce upward on the floor or down on the ceiling of a floor. But this ball also has the ability to cross the floor or ceiling if given circumstances. The rule is that the ball will only bounce (if it does) on the floor or ceiling of the floor where it is at the moment (not in the space between them wich is the floor itself), and if it crosses for example the ceiling and goes upstairs, the inertia will take it to the roof of that new floor (target). Then it could bounce there or cross that roof at first touch and move to the next floor. That is, if the price comes from below, the ceiling of new floor to which it accedes will be the target Let's see the chart: The price (ball) reaches the roof of the first floor and does not bounce, it crosses. We have left the first floor behind and we are already on the second floor. What happens here? The price begins to rebound on the roof and the floor several times until finally it crosses the ceiling and goes to the third floor. The price has already left the second floor and will not be able to cross it back until it reaches the roof of the third floor (target).What do we have on the second floor? A FLAG. Which are its limits? The floor and ceiling of the second floor. Floors and ceilings are FLs and can be FTRs, S/R, etc, too. I supose that at he left the ceilings and floors are respected, too. What happens on the third floor? Reaches the ceiling and directly crosses (line 3) to the fourth floor, so it must go to the ceilong of that new floor (target). What happens on the fourth floor? The ball (price) bounces a couple of times on ceiling and floor and crosses the floor returning to the floor below (third floor). As I said before, the price can only bounce off the floor and ceiling. As it comes from the ceiling, where could it bounce? On the floor, which is in turn the second floor ceiling. And so on. So what conclusion can we draw from this symmetry? The price will always bounce off the ceiling or floor and not anywhere else inside the floor. Therefore, WE ONLY MUST PLAN THE TRADES AT FLOOR OR CEILING OF THE FLOOR IN WHICH WE FIND US. OR WHAT IS THE SAME, IN THE FLs, FTR, etc. The engulf of one floor with a Flag inside will shoe us intentions to continue in the direction of the engulf. In the future, this structure of floors will be respected and the importance of each floor depend on what you have in the past on that floor PD: It is possible that everything I have said is nothing but nonsense. Where there has been no retrace to pick them up. Be careful, in some instances what looks clean may not be. For example a big pole down which looks like it has left clean orders at a decision above, may have retraced. So get all the info possible in LTFs To think about clean orders, turn your mind to CP. True CP (not stacked) acts as a pole on the opposing move because any orders have been picked up (for reasons discussed all over RTM). Also, a flag may look completed in one scale, but there are often more MPLs on tiny scales. One must adjust analysis and expectations for this Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. In order to do so, they cannot move the market fast, otherwise everyone will just buy and price shoots too far - REMEMBER: For ITs to buy they need sellers and vice versa. Therefore from my graph: 1. I as IT moved the price slowly back up to the supply (with CP) and added SELL orders throughout the CP. 2. As the price reached the previous H & S (QM) level, i let it stall for a while making them believe I am adding more buy orders at the same time Sellers see Double Top pattern and are ready to sell. 3. At the supply QM level, I remove my buy orders and price moves down making Sellers jumping on the wagon. 4. I suprise them and push the price back to FO level (There are now greedy buyers on board, and Double top sellers on board + This last push up to FO also invites late buyers as they believe its the start of new "trend") I noticed, it was easier to make this chart than reading the chart from MT4 lol... We read PA, and use it extensively for our trading. But the market is moved by people. Most of these people we see over and over again, making plays from the same book all week long. Sometimes though, a new player will dump a ton of orders into the market; more than the ITs are willing to cover, and a level will break. Sometimes an IT will himself make a slip and accidentally break a level. Sometimes an IT will break a level just to mess with us lot's brains. These events are extremely rare, but they do happen. If they didn't happen, we could go all in on every trade, and soon find ourselves as rich as the Rothschilds! It's due to this risk of false PA that we only risk a small percent of our accounts on any trade or set of correlated trades. Note: Should the ITs ever change their rulebook, don't worry. To answer a PM I got, which was "Is there any way to know how far will the retrace will happen after the break of the level?" No.It can retrace to any set of clean orders in the zone it's traveled through. Ideally it will travel all the way back for a QM at the MPL, or even break the H/L for a DM, but it often only retraces a short way, leaving the clean orders beyond for later. At each minor level it retraces to, we can take confirmed LTF trades, taking some profits to cover losses, letting some run to the HTF target, should this be the depth of the RT Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. The following user(s) said Thank You: PinkPanter , cuimingzhao Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 18 Jul 2017 05:37 #2744 Rinehart --> Away Associate Trader Posts: 450 Thank you received: 927 PinkPanter wrote: the other BIG mistery is NEWS releases, who buys in that milisecond, so the price spike up directly into supply and reverses and goes in other direction than big news pole? if they know that price will bounce why they buy it?? PinkPanter, news releases works almost exactly the opposite way most people imagine. The big spikes that happen right before and during a news release are rarely caused by ITs dropping massive orders and then reversing their orders with even more massive orders the other way. What often happens is that some IT's (since ITs trade different time frames too) remove their orders from the market. This causes a vacuum of orderflow where price moves to find new equilibrium. When we are talking about a spike to supply, there was more demand than supply once IT pulled their orders. This allows the sharp move higher to strong supply or an area with lots of retail buy stops (because IT takes opposite of retail). Then price falls because of overwhelming supply. I think there is a lot of ambiguity in this diagram and a lot of variables too. Firstly, is this an MPL of a FL or is a QM in a swing as a reaction to another FL/kink? If it is a QM, then price can make a diamond up to the MPL of a FL from above. The problem with diamonds and QM is that you can rarely find an engulf which hasn't hit its target so you have to gamble on them a little bit, i think. So, knowing that you can't find a engulf which hasn't hit its target nowadays, its definitely almost impossible to take gambling out of equation even when you trade BSZ. You have two important things to think about when you try to score your BSZ trade: - FLAG(BSZ) not touching the kink (so you can take FTB to that kink), and an engulf down (which is impossible to find it nowadays). So basically, from what i have seen in my study in forex tester, i cant expect more than 60% P/L ratio on these things and often the initial R is less than 1:1 because your kink is larger than your BSZ FO zone. If you want high R you have to be more agressive and i dont know, i think P/L ratio will drop down even more. Maybe i do something wrong but this is how i see it now. We have to deal with losses. I think i do something wrong, but so far this is how i see it. And regarding range filling, how can you expect for a range to be filled if you have no engulf which hasn't hit its target, you are not at the QM zone, and even if you are, price can make a diamond to an MPL of the FL from above which is 2TB to it now, so its risky. Although I know where the levels are located, I only trade the best ones. But I need to know where price is coming from and which level is in control on my higher scale(s). I never think in terms of QM, DM, CanCan anymore as it s only a byproduct of the order flow and manipulation. This has slightly changed in recent times with another method the ITs use for entries and targets as well. Everything in between the above and below level in that scale is a potential range to be filled. I base nearly my entire price reading on this. I use smaller scales to ride it up or down. Although I know where the levels are located, I only trade the best ones. But I need to know where price is coming from and which level is in control on my higher scale(s). I never think in terms of QM, DM, CanCan anymore as it s only a byproduct of the order flow and manipulation. In the picture IF posted, when he talked about dealers (or IT) that needs to fill a range, he most likely refer to a HTF range as depicted in my drawing below. So imagine on a HTF scale, price has already established a range from A to B. So when IT bring the price back to C, the movement from B to C is called 'filling the range'. Likewise, movement of C to D, and then from D back to E, are all called filling the range. Best regards Astro Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 25 Oct 2017 22:26 #3017 einrikr --> Offline Trader Posts: 203 Thank you received: 215 May I have a crack on this? I hope I understand you correctly, but here goes: The FL can only be drawn if price hit it's target means that if price doesn't retrace back far enough, it's not hitting the FL below and therefore it's no new FL but price just goes beyond it. There are several targets for price in several stages of it moving. The target for a new FL, is the FL below (or above) it and that has to be hit. I hope that clarifies it, and that I'm explaining it correctly! Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. At point 1 price engulfs a LFL - which at that point is PA (an engulf which didn’t hit its target (2) So, we will now look for an opportunity to short at the UFL. 2.) At point 1 price engulfs a LFL, retraces just a little bit and hits its target (2) straight after – which means a new UFL (3) is formed. I think this is what dengaima means – for an engulf to be tradeable we need the engulf to not hit its target. (However, price failed to pick up the orders in the UFL (4) so I guess these will always be attractive for the ITs?) 3.) In the 3rd scenario we have an engulf of the LFL (2) at (5) – so again we look for a short opportunity at the UFL (3) But we have to be more careful with this UFL. Why is that? That is because we have left unfilled orders at the UFL (4). Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 14 Nov 2017 19:00 #3156 HCDE --> Offline Associate Trader Posts: 471 Thank you received: 648 I tried to take the exercise on and began to elaborate some scenarios. NB: i had to reproduce IF's drawing and made a clean version of it i join to the post in case other people want to use it for their scenarios It made me realize something important that i missed. I tried many times to spot engulfs into a FL (opposed to engulf of a FL). But when doing that i was considering in the same way a break in between two targets Inside the FL than a break in between the S/R kink of the FL and the first iLS. This is a mistake, because by breaking S/R kink and reaching first iLS, price reaches it's TG and therefore validates a new UFL Any break of that UFL is actually PA UP... So in that situation we shouldn't expect price to retrace to the UFL we came from and then get further into the LFL... Lesson learned. We have a beautiful PAZ formed right on the base of a 4hr resistance/supply area, within the PAZ I have noted a demand zone which was touched @ blue 1,2 and then spike @ 3 (A question here one could ask is all of the buy orders consumed?) I am under no illusion with this as I know this is after the fact and hindsight is 20/20, I was just wondering if there were any other entries or anything that may improve my analysis. I start with this visible swing low on H4, see point 1 on chart below: you may argue that 1 is a reaction to FL-A, but most traders who doesn't understand FL would look at 1 and think that's a support and therefore place buy orders there, therefore to break this swing low, it would still require a significantly large sell order. But I have also found several interesting elements: I saw a smaller FL-C which breaks into the CPAZ, so this can be an important FL. Then I saw a DP (green box) which delineated the upper edge of FL-B, and from my observations so far, in order to confirm PA to the north, we need price to engulf not only FL-B, but also the DP that defined the edge of it. If you think about it, even though we call FL-B a flag limit, but on smaller scale it's actually a flag, and then the DP became the flag limit of Flag-B!. Then I also saw a QM level inside FL-B, and I want to see what was responsible for breaking this QM level too. Fast forward to 14 November 2017, where all of these elements were broken. I see FL-C being engulfed by FL-D QM-level being engulfed by FL-E DP being engulfed by FL-F So we now see how price reacting to each of these FLs. Chart below showed price reacting to the upper edge of FL-F and bounced upwards Then on 19 November, price plunged into FL-E and bounced upwards strongly Then on 21 November, price hit FL-D twice, and the second time it 'almost' engulfed it. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You If 29 Mar 2018 05:50 #3444 bobyv87 --> Offline Associate Trader Posts: 326 Thank you received: 311 Its very difficult, if not impossible to give signals using RTM reading way. Why? Because even the right level can be FOed. So, knowing that, we always should have hard stops somewhere, but we don't wait for the hard stop to be hit, instead, after price break our level (fail level), we exit right at the next chance, when price bounce back to our fail level so we can exit without loss. Now, imagine that every level could have inside a few fresh orders. Would you wait always for MPLs inside each levels? If yes, you will miss a lot of opportunities. Would you wait lower than MPL? Maybe you wouldn't have the chance to exit at BE if your level fails. So, you have to take quick decisions, even if you have a good level and a good signal. At the same LSK IF can take a BE or a small profit, but in the same time others can take losses. Because of these multiple factors, its very difficult to do that. And imagine how much pressure you can put on IF with that.
